#2242. Champions League draw: Arsenal to renew Mourinho rivalry with Real Madrid tie

Arsenal will host old nemesis José Mourinho’s Real Madrid in the league phase of the Champions League.

Mourinho, the former Chelsea, Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur manager, will return to London to resume hostilities against last season’s beaten finalists.

Other reunions from Thursday’s draw include Manchester City travelling to Barcelona, to whom they last week sold Rodri, and Liverpool visiting Inter Milan, who have signed Curtis Jones.

Arsenal will also travel to Harry Kane’s Bayern Munich, while United will host the Germans as well on their Champions League return in a repeat of the legendary 1999 final. Michael Carrick’s side will also visit Cesc Fàbregas’s Como.

Mourinho last managed at the Emirates Stadium in March 2021, barely a month before his sacking by Spurs.

During his two spells as Chelsea manager, Mourinho famously had run-ins with Arsenal’s Arsène Wenger.

Mourinho called Wenger a “specialist in failure” after the Frenchman failed to add to his three Premier League titles following his Portuguese counterpart’s arrival in London in 2004.

Last season, Mikel Arteta finally ended Arsenal’s long wait to be crowned champions of England but agonisingly missed out on European glory.

Verdict Premier League champions should not be daunted by any game, but Real Madrid – with Mourinho in control – has the feel of a defining match of the group stage. Facing Kane in Munich does not seem any easier. Some tough assignments here including a trip to Napoli but the pot-four teams seem straightforward for Mikel Arteta.

Verdict Playing against the European champions and travelling to Barcelona will be a true test of how much progress Enzo Maresca has made in the short time he has been at the Etihad Stadium. City’s other games do not look easy either but they should be defeating teams such as Sporting Lisbon and Porto – at least they would be expected to under Pep Guardiola.

Verdict The San Siro was where Arne Slot began to turn results around last season and Iraola getting a win there would be a big statement. Atlético staged a comeback at Anfield in 2020 and the repeat fixture will be tight. But there are enough winnable games there for Liverpool to reach the next round.

Verdict They will face a wall of noise in Istanbul when they play Galatasaray, but Villa will look to get points from the game. There are some tasty destinations for travelling fans and getting results there will ease the pressure on the match against PSG, who have been rattled by Villa before but remain a difficult opponent. The Nou Camp is a place where momentum can change in a season – for good or bad.

Verdict The repeat of the 1999 final is the standout fixture, but Michael Carrick should be looking beyond that match for the points needed to progress. He has been given a tough set of away games to navigate. They are winnable but difficult. So those games at Old Trafford will be very important.

That brings our coverage of the Champions League draw to an end, as the 36 teams found which eight teams they will be facing in the league phase of this season’s tournament. Thanks for joining us!

The league phase will kick off on 8 September and will be wrapped up after all teams play at the same time on 27 January.

The top eight teams of the league phase progress to the last 16 automatically, while teams that finish between ninth and 24th will be forced to navigate a play-off tie to reach the knockout stages.

This season is the third under the new format, with a league phase instead of a group stage, and Uefa has confirmed that fixtures that have taken place in the league phase of the two previous seasons cannot be repeated this time around.

For example, Liverpool cannot host Real Madrid in the league phase this term after welcoming the 15-time European champions to Anfield at this stage of the previous two campaigns. Andoni Iraola’s side could, however, travel to the Bernabeu for an away meeting with Madrid.

Similarly, Arsenal will not be travelling to San Siro to face Inter, but could host the Serie A champions at the Emirates.

Arsenal finished top of the league phase last season after winning all eight fixtures and it resulted in a favourable run to the final, facing Bayer Leverkusen, Sporting and Atletico Madrid.

Liverpool, meanwhile, topped the league phase in the 2024-25 campaign – the first season with the new format – but fell at the first hurdle in the knockout stages after being drawn against Paris St-Germain.

The Ligue 1 side have proven that it’s not essential to be firing the whole way through the tournament, finishing 15th and 11th in the league phase in the last two seasons but going on to lift the trophy on both occasions.

#2241. Bolton Wanderers are giving Wrexham real transfer envy with £0 signing

Sam Dalby is fast becoming one of the more underrated strikers in the Championship today at Bolton Wanderers, which must be a real gut-punch to those associated with Wrexham.

The 26-year-old was brought into the EFL with the Red Dragons, but was a mere squad option during their National League and League Two promotion campaigns, to the point where the club decided to loan him out in the final year of his deal in the 2024/25 term.

At that point, Wrexham were a League One side, and showing no signs of slowing down. Many felt that they were rapidly outgrowing Dalby, but the towering frontman was about to prove those critics wrong.

Indeed, a brilliant loan spell at Dundee United in the Scottish Premiership made Wrexham second-guess their decision that summer, and when they tried to offer him a new deal, it was Dalby's turn to turn them down.

Now he's at Bolton, thriving, and those at the Racecourse are regretting not using him as much while he was their player.

Looking at Dalby now, it's easy to blame Wrexham for mishandling him. But it was never as easy as that. The frontman arrived at the Racecourse as a 22-year-old after a nine-goal campaign at Southend United.

He wasn't exactly pulling up trees beforehand, and he was joining a side that had Paul Mullin leading the line and Ollie Palmer beside him. It was always going to be a struggle to dislodge those from the starting eleven at National League level.

Football League World has asked AI to rank the top 25 most demanding fanbases in British football right now

Dalby started just nine times in the 2022/23 campaign, but did get off the bench another 32 times. He was rarely seen as a sporadic fringe player, just not a regular starter.

That changed a little bit in League Two, though, especially in the first half of the season. Both he and Palmer rotated alongside Mullin, and he started 14 league games that year.

The only issue was that he only scored once in League Two that year, and when Wrexham went out and brought in Jack Marriott and Steven Fletcher midway through the season, he became even more of an afterthought than he was in the National League, only making two appearances in the final 13 games.

Hindsight is a brilliant thing, because there weren't many against the idea of loaning Dalby out in the summer of 2024.

After barely featuring in League Two, his minutes were only going to decrease in League One, and it seemed a given that the then-24-year-old would just see out his final 12 months under contract at Wrexham before moving on the following summer.

However, after scoring 10 goals by January 2nd in the SPL with Dundee United, who weren't expecting to be in the midst of a push for Europe in their first season back in the top flight, Wrexham quickly realised that they may have made a mistake.

Five players, five careers. Name them from the clubs they played for.

Each day there are five current or former EFL players to identify. For each one you’ll see their senior clubs in the order they played for them. Loan spells are left out.

You get four guesses per player. Every wrong guess unlocks a clue: first their position, then their nationality, then their initials.

Get it first time for 4 points, then 3, 2 and 1. The best possible score is 20. A new set of players arrives at midnight.

As stated in their retained list at the end of the 2024/25 campaign, they offered Dalby a new contract in January of that season with the hopes of extending his time at the club so they could, at the very least, profit from this breakout year.

The striker turned that down, though, and after ending the campaign with 15 goals in 35 league games, helping Dundee United finish fourth and qualify for the qualification rounds of the UEFA Conference League that year, he became a free agent.

Dalby had more than earned the four-year deal handed to him by Bolton ahead of last season. The Trotters had eyes on the Championship and, initially, the then-25-year-old was seen as a squad player to help that happen.

Like at Wrexham, Dalby was a victim of a red-hot striker in the opening months of the 2025/26 campaign, as Hull City loanee Mason Burstow scored seven in his first 11 games. In fact, the towering frontman started just four league games before mid-January, and Bolton picked up just one point in those.

From the 1-0 derby win at Wigan Athletic on January 17, something switched, and Dalby became practically undroppable. Even if Burstow started games, it was often as a two with the 26-year-old, who would be the hold-up man to bring others into the game.

He scored 10 league goals in just over 2,300 minutes, but crucially, missed the last two games through injury, which put his status in the play-offs in jeopardy.

However, that became quite the masterstroke for Steven Schumacher during their run to Wembley and their subsequent promotion. Dalby came off the bench in all three play-off matchups and changed the game in each.

Against Stockport County in the final, he came on with a little under an hour remaining, with the score at 1-1, and two minutes later, Bolton took the lead after his deft touch sent Amario Cozier-Duberry's away, and Kyle Wootton deflected the cross into his own net.

He then made it 3-1 with an overhead kick, and was, effectively, the game-changer in Bolton's promotion to the Championship.

Even despite his excellence in the play-off final, it was almost universally agreed that Bolton would need a new striker in the summer. Max Dean seemed to be the favourite, but after his move broke down, the Trotters could only really bring in more supporting members for Dalby.

The 26-year-old has thrived as the starting striker this year, though. He's continued to be one of the best linkmen in the EFL and has more than a handful of goals to show for it, too.

How many goals do you think Sam Dalby will score in the Championship this season? Let us know in the comments.

And, crucially, at this moment in time, he's scored more league goals this season than anyone in the Wrexham squad. For what is his first season in the second tier, it's not been bad going so far.

Now, he's one of Bolton's most important players, and one that you would imagine needs to remain fit for the Trotters to stand a chance at establishing themselves in the Championship, which isn't something anyone associated with Wrexham would have imagined back in the summer of 2024 after loaning him out to Dundee United.

#2240. AI predicts Sheffield Wednesday's League One finish under Dave Challinor

Sheffield Wednesday have their man, as Dave Challinor was officially confirmed as the new Owls boss earlier this week.

The 51-year-old seemed almost destined for the post at Hillsborough ever since his hugely successful stint at Stockport County came to an end following defeat in the play-off final against Bolton Wanderers.

County's CEO Simon Wilson departed at the end of the season to become the new sporting director at Wednesday, and now the two will work together once more in South Yorkshire to get over the line and into the second tier after falling short at Stockport.

The Hatters finished third in consecutive League One campaigns under Challinor, who'd overseen their rise from the National League to the third tier in the four-and-a-half years he spent in charge.

Five players, five careers. Name them from the clubs they played for.

Each day there are five current or former EFL players to identify. For each one you’ll see their senior clubs in the order they played for them. Loan spells are left out.

You get four guesses per player. Every wrong guess unlocks a clue: first their position, then their nationality, then their initials.

Get it first time for 4 points, then 3, 2 and 1. The best possible score is 20. A new set of players arrives at midnight.

Promotion will be the goal, and this demanding fanbase, who called for Henrik Pedersen's head despite sitting eighth in the division at the time, will be wanting it at the quickest possible moment, but what does AI think?

Henrik Pedersen's dismissal came after just 11 games of the League One campaign. At that time, Wednesday were two points removed from a play-off place with a game in hand, and had won games 7-2 and 5-0 against Bromley and AFC Wimbledon, respectively.

Ultimately, Challinor isn't coming in to a club in crisis, even if just two points in a run of games against Notts County, Doncaster Rovers, Cambridge United and Blackpool isn't exactly play-off form.

The ex-Stockport boss has 33 league games to help gain, at worst, two points on the side in sixth place, or six points on his former side, who occupy the second automatic promotion spot, which seems a doable task.

According to ChatGPT, he'll succeed in the former, but fall just short of finishing in the top two. Indeed, AI feels that Sheffield Wednesday will finish 4th this season under Challinor.

Do you think Sheffield Wednesday can get promoted this season under Dave Challinor? Let us know in the comments.

While that wouldn't be the ideal scenario for some Owls fans, they can feel reassured that ChatGPT went on to state that it predicts play-off success at Wembley, with Challinor's recent history of struggling to get through the postseason at Stockport not bleeding into his tenure at Hillsborough.

Ultimately, the appointment of Dave Challinor won't just mean that Sheffield Wednesday will stroll up the League One table and finish in the top two with ease. The 51-year-old has good credentials, but even he knows how unforgiving this division can be.

Additionally, this is a job like no other for Challinor. The Owls are a giant of English football that, ultimately, the likes of AFC Fylde, Hartlepool United and Stockport aren't.

Especially at Stockport, there wasn't as much fan pressure if things weren't going as well. Ultimately, he's brought the club closer to the Championship than they have been for 25 years, and that gave him plenty of credit in the bank.

At Sheffield Wednesday, though, he'll be under pressure to oversee winning performances in front of 30,000 at Hillsborough every other week and packed away ends elsewhere, and if bad results creep in, as they did under Pedersen, it won't take long for negativity to set in.

This is a job that Challinor has earned, but there's still a tiny bit of scepticism surrounding his fit from AI, hence the haste in putting them amongst the top two immediately.

Challinor was in the stands at Hillsborough on Sunday in their draw against Blackpool, observing and writing notes. He'll have plenty of time to get to work and implement some of those ideas in the coming weeks.

Wednesday are in action against Oldham Athletic in the FA Cup first round on Sunday in front of the TV cameras, giving the Owls a chance to showcase any changes immediately in front of a national audience.

From then, though, they have an EFL Trophy matchup at Accrington Stanley, which will serve almost as a free hit with the Owls already through to the knockout phase, and then likely a nine-day break due to the upcoming international window.

AI has had its say on which clubs are currently the biggest sleeping giants outside the Premier League

Dave Challinor's side haven't had their game against Plymouth Argyle postponed just yet, but it will likely happen. Kieran Morrison has already been called up for Northern Ireland, and their two games over the last break had to be rearranged, too.

So, with only one "meaningful" game against an out-of-form League Two opponent in his first 17 days officially in charge, it presents a good opportunity to stamp his authority on this new side.

All eyes will be on Oakwell on November 20, as Wednesday travel to Barnsley in what could set the tone for a promotion charge. Perhaps then, a fourth-placed prediction could be selling them a little short.

#2239. Rangers star wanted for permanent transfer as current boss makes feelings clear

Jim Goodwin admits Dundee United would jump at the chance to sign Lyall Cameron permanently from Rangers.

The midfielder has impressed since moving to Tannadice on loan, establishing himself as an important part of Goodwin’s side.

Cameron joined Rangers from Dundee in the summer of 2025 but struggled to establish himself as a regular at Ibrox. He spent the second half of last season on loan at Aberdeen before joining Dundee United on another temporary spell.

Cameron remains under contract with Rangers until 2029, meaning his parent club retain control over his long-term future. However, Goodwin has made no secret of his desire to keep the midfielder if an opportunity arises.

#2238. Manchester United confirmed lineup: Amad & Yoro return to starting lineup

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur return from the international break with plenty to prove when they meet at Old Trafford on Saturday.

Michael Carrick’s side have won just once in their last four domestic matches since beating Ipswich 5-2. A Carabao Cup defeat to Brighton was followed by a loss to 10-man Manchester City, before Manchester United drew with Everton and Fulham. Matheus Cunha’s late equaliser at Fulham rescued a point, but Manchester United still sit 12th.

Roberto De Zerbi’s side are bottom of the Premier League with only two points from their opening five games. Spurs have failed to score in four of those matches, while defeats against Aston Villa and Newcastle have added to the pressure.

Michael Carrick has named his starting eleven for the clash at Old Trafford, with Kobbie Mainoo and Youri Tielemans partnering in midfield as United look to get their season back on track.

Senne Lammens starts in goal, with Leny Yoro, Lisandro Martinez, Harry Maguire and Luke Shaw forming the back four. Carrick has opted for Mainoo and Tielemans in the middle, with Amad Diallo, Bruno Fernandes and Matheus Cunha tasked with supporting Bryan Mbeumo up front.

Leny Yoro had a brilliant international break where he made his debut for France. His performance on debut was enough for Zidane to praise the debutant.

Amad, after missing the start of the season with an injury, returns straightaway to the team.

Carlos Baleba starts on the bench and is expected to make his debut today. Marcus Rashford is also on the bench alongside Shea Lacey.

Lammens; Yoro, Martinez, Maguire, Shaw; Mainoo, Tielemans; Amad, Bruno Fernandes, Mbeumo; Cunha.

Mbeumo gets his place through the middle, while Amad and Cunha start on the wing after scoring the late equaliser against Fulham. Fernandes will be expected to start producing the numbers from last season after a lackluster start to the season, except against Ipswich, before the international break.

United need a response after a difficult run, but Tottenham arrive under pressure of their own. With both sides desperate for points, the starting lineups set the stage for an important afternoon at Old Trafford.

#2237. Tottenham's hidden West Ham, Manor Solomon clause takes new twist

West Ham's decision to acquire Manor Solomon on a permanent transfer from Tottenham Hotspur over the summer raised initial eyebrows and is now coming under intensifying scrutiny, leaving questions to be asked over both his long-term future and a certain clause within the deal.

The Hammers' reintroduction to life in the Championship following 14 largely-successful years at Premier League level has not quite followed the script, having headed into the campaign as overwhelming title favourites.

West Ham find themselves positioned in eighth place after 14 games, however, and recently relieved Nuno Espirito Santo of his duties in the wake of successive defeats against two promotion rivals in Southampton and West Bromwich Albion before appointing Scott Parker.

The ex-Hammers and England international midfielder's tenure got off to a shaky start on Tuesday evening when the East Londoners could only muster a 3-3 draw away to Cardiff City, albeit with a remarkable recovery from a shock 3-0 deficit at half time, and it will be interesting to see what direction of travel they enjoy under the stewardship of a three-time second-tier promotion-winner with serious skin in the game within the club.

And exactly what lies ahead for Solomon, who has predominantly fallen short of delivering the desired impact upon his switch across London, only remains to be seen, putting the microscope on the deal that took the winger to the Championship in the first place.

West Ham shelled out an initial £5 million figure to secure Solomon's services on a permanent basis and agreed a three-year contract with the former Leeds United loan star, with the deal capable of rising to £7 million subject to various add-on criteria.

It's only likely, of course, that some criteria pertains to the Hammers' ongoing promotion charge, and though they are only just inside the play-offs at this moment in time, it's hard to look past Scott Parker's men making up relative ground as the campaign toils on and achieving a top-two finish.

Another clause, however, is far more interesting, and provides an intriguing discussion point amid increasing criticism of Solomon's acquisition in East London.

It was widely reported that Spurs, where the 27-year-old wide-man made just six competitive appearances across an injury-plagued spell of three years and just as many loans away from the club, included a 10% sell-on clause for any future fee that West Ham collect further down the line.

These seven players won't be available as Scott Parker looks for his first win as West Ham boss against Blackburn

Solomon's resale value, mind you, is open to debate, and his stock has declined after previously lighting up the Championship on loan at Leeds to inspire their 100-point title triumph with 10 goals and 12 assists during the 2024/25 campaign.

With the West Ham attacker struggling to find his rhythm in the opening months, he's only earning the ever-growing ire of the London Stadium faithful while posing questions about his price-tag, the club's decision to complete the signing and exactly what Spurs could end up getting out of their sell-on clause.

Solomon has previous pedigree in European competition with Shakhtar Dontesk and tangible top-flight experience from spells at Fulham, Villarreal and Fiorentina alongside a strong second-tier reputation from his aforementioned exploits in West Yorkshire, but none of that has been translated to claret colours since making the move to West Ham.

He started off in style by finding the back of the net on debut during West Ham's 2-2 opening-weekend draw at Burnley before adding a goal and an assist to his name when the Hammers ran riot over Wrexham in a 6-0 rout on September 11.

Solomon would then set up another in West Ham's next league fixture away to fierce rivals Millwall a week later, though it's now been a month-and-a-half - or six matches - since Solomon last provided a direct goal involvement.

For a player of the ex-Shakhtar and Spurs winger's pedigree, the lack of production has left Hammers supporters frustrated as he continues to flatter to deceive.

Notably off the pace in his side's most recent draw at Cardiff, in which he lasted 70 minutes before being hauled off for £18 million summer signing Edvin Austbo as the visitors chased an all-important equaliser, the signing is now at real risk of not working out for all parties - leaving many to wonder why Spurs even added a sell-on clause in the first place.

Unfortunately for Solomon, it would appear as though West Ham fans have already made their minds up and the winger now faces a losing battle to regain the support of the London Stadium crowd.

His anonymous display against the Bluebirds has seemingly provided the final nail in the coffin for some, with many supporters taking to social media in recent times to make their thoughts clear.

This one fan, who was far from the only punter to share such a sentiment, doesn't wish to see the ex-Spurs wide-man in a Hammers shirt again.

He's far from popular in East London right now, which was displayed here.

Some would argue this particular claim is too harsh, although it's a damning indictment of just how unpopular Solomon has become merely months after joining the promotion-chasing side.

West Ham fans, do you think there's any way back for Manor Solomon? What have you made of the winger's start to life in East London? Let us know your thoughts in the comments below!

Solomon still has time to turn it around, of course, but many West Ham supporters don't want him to be given that and have even urged for his contract to be ripped up already.

This fan hasn't been as vocal about Solomon, but is still onside with the general consensus that Austbo, having arrived as one of the most expensive signings in Championship history, deserves a run of games ahead of his left-flank counterpart.

The pacey Norweigan was much livelier against Cardiff after coming on for the closing stages and has the same number of goal contributions - two goals and two assists apiece - in 667 fewer minutes of league action.

Indeed, Austbo has started on just two occasions as Solomon continues to fall short of providing the goods as a consistent starter, and it only remains to be seen whether Parker will take to the tricky 21-year-old more than his predecessor.

West Ham fans will hope that's the case, though, and if Austbo seizes any forthcoming opportunities for a regular run in the side then it's hard to see how Solomon will make good of his transfer and become any sort of successful signing under Parker.

Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur returned from the international break with plenty to prove after a disastrous start to the season.

United arrived with just one win, while Tottenham came to Old Trafford without a win.

Both teams had half-chances in the first half but little to show for them. Tottenham had the better chances with chances for Dominic Solanke, Connor Gallagher and Kudus, but none could take advantage of them.

Manchester United came close in the first half to score after Bryan Mbeumo raced towards the goal on a counter-attack to find Amad. He had a difficult shot, and eventually the shot was too weak to cause any damage. The first-half display was met by boos from the Old Trafford crowd at half-time and during the first half as well.

Solanke had another chance at the start of the second half but put it over the top, amid a wrestle with Lisandro Martinez in the six-yard box. It was United, however, who started the second half with promise.

Substitutions by Michael Carrick around the hour mark made the difference as United showed intent before Mbeumo got the goal off Cunha’s low cross. Luke Shaw was at the end of a scuffle with Bentancur, who was shown a red card for headbutting Shaw.

United failed to capitalize on their one-man advantage and seemed to sit on their 1-0 lead, but Solanke punished them with a header to level the game in injury time. The draw left United with just 6 points off their first six games. The result leaves United with their worst start in 40 years.

#2235. Turki Alalshikh blame rejected as Derby County crisis deepens

It has been a nightmare start to the season for Derby County in the Championship.

After missing out on the play-offs on the final day of last season, Derby would have been hoping to challenge for promotion once again this campaign, but John Eustace's men currently find themselves at the wrong end of the table.

Derby owner David Clowes has made no secret of his desire to bring fresh investment into the club in recent years, and it looked as though a cash injection was imminent after Saudi billionaire Turki Alalshikh agreed to purchase a controlling stake in the club.

The proposed deal had been given approval by the EFL and the Independent Football Regulator, but Alalshikh unexpectedly withdrew from the takeover in August, claiming that, as the campaign had already started, he had "no time to prepare the team or the club for the season ahead".

While the Rams went on to make further signings after Alalshikh's takeover deal collapsed, including the permanent addition of midfielder David Ozoh for a fee of around £4 million, head coach John Eustace later claimed that the saga caused the club to lose "a lot of momentum on players that we were looking at".

After the off-field drama over the summer, Derby have made a disastrous start to the season on the pitch, and they head into the November international break sitting in the Championship relegation zone, with pressure building on Eustace as increasing numbers of supporters call for a managerial change.

When asked if Alalshikh's takeover falling through at the last minute is to blame for the club's poor start, FLW's Derby County fan pundit Shaun Woodward admitted that it is a contributing factor, as well as the recent injury crisis, but he insisted that a managerial change is the only way to get the Rams out of their current predicament.

"There is definitely an element of blame on Turki Alalshikh for pulling out so late in the day, but we can't be pinning it all on the takeover," Shaun told FLW.

"John Eustace still has a more than capable squad at his disposal.

"The majority of that squad was good enough to get us to an eighth-placed finish last season.

"Yes, it might have affected the transfers he had pencilled in, and we had to then go for plan B or plan C transfers, but the nucleus of that squad is still far too good to be in the position that we find ourselves in now.

"Yes, you can also blame injuries to our backline, but, again, the players that have stepped in should be doing better, they are still Championship players.

"They are not covering themselves in any glory whatsoever, and you can say the same about Eustace and his staff because they haven't been able to motivate the players, their tactics seem wrong, he doesn't sound very inspiring in his post-match interviews, and he looks defeated.

"The players look lost out on the pitch, but, all of that said, you can blame Eustace as much as you want, and he will lose his job because of this as the buck stops with him, the players have let him down massively as well.

"The last couple of performances especially at Millwall and at home to Norwich, the players have downed tools, they have given up.

"They are very much playing in individual mode, where they don't want to be made the scapegoat, they are hiding on the pitch, we can all see it as fans.

"No one is looking like they really care, and it's sad to see because there's still a nucleus of players out on that pitch that should be far better than 23rd in the league with the lowest goals scored and the highest goals conceded.

"We're not creating anything, we're gifting teams goal after goal, so I think there's an element of everything involved here.

"Yes, the takeover didn't help, maybe the transfers weren't the ones we wanted necessarily, but I still felt we had a good enough squad.

"Injuries haven't helped the backline, but the players that have come in haven't stepped up, and the more experienced players in our squad haven't led by example.

"It's just been a shambles, and, let's be real, the warning signs were there in pre-season, we looked lathargic and unfit, and that's carried on into the season.

"Until we get a new manager, I just can't see it changing, and, even then, it's going to be tough for someone to come in with the current group.

"The confidence is rock bottom, someone is going to have to come in and change formation, change personnel, rip up the script and start again because right now, we're only heading one way and that's League One."

While Alalshikh agreed a deal to invest in Derby and went through the EFL and IFR approval processes, Clowes and Eustace must have known that there was always a chance his takeover could collapse, particularly given that his previous interest in other Championship clubs, such as Bristol City and Millwall, had failed to progress.

Alalshikh's late withdrawal would inevitably have caused some disruption to the Rams' transfer plans, but Eustace still has a competitive squad at his disposal, which includes many of those who helped the club to an eighth-placed finish last season.

Can Turki Alalshikh's failed takeover be blamed for Derby County's poor start? Tell us in the comments below!

With that in mind, there is little excuse for Derby to be in their current position, even taking their extensive injury list into account, and it is difficult not to feel that Eustace will be fortunate to survive the upcoming international break.

We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful.

#2234. Michael Carrick reacts to Man Utd boos after Tottenham draw

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Michael Carrick admitted Manchester United’s 1-1 draw with Tottenham Hotspur was a painful result, after his side failed to protect the lead against 10-man Tottenham at Old Trafford.

Manchester United looked set to claim three points when Bryan Mbeumo scored in the second half off Cunha’s low cross, but Dominic Solanke’s late equaliser in injury time left Carrick facing more questions on United’s performance and his future.

Speaking to BBC Match of the Day, the United manager felt his players improved after the break but failed to handle the situation when victory was within reach.

“It was a mixed game. We found it tough to start with. For a number of reasons, we were not quite there. You could see it was a challenging time,” Carrick said.

“But the lads grew into the game, in the second half I thought we were better in everything. To get the game as we wanted it, in such a good position – we should see it through. We have to manage those situations.”

United have now conceded two late goals that have cost them valuable points, something Carrick believes has made their position look worse than it might have otherwise.

Asked whether a lack of confidence had contributed to United’s slow start, he disagreed but admitted matches can quickly slip away from his side.

The boos at half-time and full-time also clearly affected him.

“It’s not nice, it hurts a lot because I care about this club. But I understand the disappointment, the reality is what it is, we need to get back to winning games.”

#2233. Bryan Mbeumo reacts to Man Utd draw with Tottenham

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Bryan Mbeumo admitted Manchester United have work to do after their frustrating 1-1 draw with Tottenham Hotspur, despite scoring a superb second-half goal at Old Trafford.

The Cameroon international put Manchester United ahead in the 73rd minute, finishing in the far corner after Matheus Cunha created the opportunity from a low cross. However, Dominic Solanke’s stoppage-time equaliser denied Michael Carrick’s side a much-needed victory, even though Tottenham had been reduced to 10 men following Rodrigo Bentancur’s red card.

Manchester United have failed to win any of their last three Premier League games against sides that have received a red card (D1 L2).

3 – Manchester United have failed to win any of their last three Premier League games against sides that have received a red card (D1 L2). Disadvantage? pic.twitter.com/DuSpvymZfu

Speaking to Sky Sports after the game, Mbeumo acknowledged that United had taken too long to find their rhythm.

“We took time to get into the game, but we played well in the second half. In the first half, that wasn’t us, we had to change. We tried to get at them,” he said.

Mbeumo recognised the threat Tottenham posed and admitted the result was disappointing, particularly given United’s position in the game before Solanke’s late goal.

“We know Spurs have good players who can be dangerous. It’s a bit disappointing, we need to work on things.”

United have struggled for consistency in the opening weeks of the season, and dropping points after taking the lead will do little to ease the pressure on Carrick. Mbeumo, however, insisted the team must look ahead rather than dwell on the setback.

“We need to keep going forward, as we have a lot of games.”

Michael Carrick was pleased with Mbeumo’s contribution, highlighting both the quality of his finish and the different roles he has played since joining United.

“Bryan’s done great. It was a fantastic finish again; he’s obviously played different roles for us but we know what he offers,” the United manager said.

“He’s got good quality and obviously the more goals he scores, the better. He’s doing really well for us.”

Mbeumo’s goal was one of the few bright moments in another difficult afternoon for United. Carrick’s team must now find a way to turn things around from here after just six points from six games.

#2231. Cherki magic helping Maresca to step out of Guardiola shadow

Rumours of Manchester City’s supposed demise without Pep Guardiola appear to be much exaggerated.

They swept past Crystal Palace at Selhurst Park with a style of play under new manager Enzo Maresca that was just as swashbuckling as under his predecessor, with Rayan Cherki playing the role of chief architect. The Frenchman’s two goals included a captivating mazy dribble, which will long be remembered by those who had the fortune to see it.

City created enough space for themselves through clever movement. With Cherki zigging one way and Phil Foden zagging the other, they created even more by dribbling past a mesmerised Palace back three that became a back five at times and still could not cope.

Erling Haaland also scored twice. Even with the creative and unpredictable talents of those behind in a four-man attacking City midfield, Haaland remains irreplaceable with his ability to convert chances.

However, this night belonged to Cherki. Guardiola chided him publicly after he set up a City goal with a “rabona” cross last season. The thrust of Guardiola’s comments were that Cherki was not Lionel Messi. Of course not, but he possesses a genius all of his own, which Maresca would surely be foolish to rein in.

The jaw-dropping splendour of Cherki’s first goal drew a collective intake of breath at Selhurst Park.

Collecting a Foden pass, he attacked the Palace area on a diagonal path, slaloming between Jaydee Canvot, Takehiro Tomiyasu and Chris Richards, before having the spatial awareness and technique to flick his left foot at the ball to send it rolling on a perpendicular trajectory past Dean Henderson.

"The man with the magic feet!"Rayan Cherki doubles Manchester City's lead with a STUNNING goal 😮‍💨 pic.twitter.com/9Zea5vFljv

An insight into Cherki’s mindset came after the match.

He said: “My performance is s---. In the first half, we didn’t find the space, I played bad. I need to show them that I want to play, I want to score. Next time I want to give the ball around more.”

Forget the words, Maresca cannot ignore the actions of a player he left on the bench against Bournemouth.

Sterner tests will come for City than against a Palace side missing key players who may or may not leave south London in the remaining days of the transfer window.

Whether Maresca will trust his forward players to express themselves as freely against their rivals for the Premier League title remains to be seen, but with Elliot Anderson providing a one-man shield behind them, City could not be stopped.

Maresca said: “For sure Rayan is happy tonight. His performance was very good and not just for his two goals. He has to press off the ball and he was in charge of [marking] Adam Wharton, so it was a complete game by him.”

Only for the first three minutes did Palace hint at a different outcome but, after shots from Eddie Nketiah and Daichi Kamada were diverted away for corners, City took control.

They took the lead in the 17th minute when the otherwise quiet Antoine Semenyo flighted a cross over the heads of everyone except the shorn locks of Haaland, whose determined header looped over Henderson and dropped in the far corner.

The only negative of Foden’s performance came in front of goal, with a ballooned shot and a mistimed header.

After Cherki’s solo masterpiece had made it 2-0, Yeremy Pino seized the next moment for his own with a stunning free-kick that flicked the crossbar, then the back of City keeper Gianluigi Donnarumma before finally dropping over the line.

"This is a good a free-kick as you're likely to see this season!" Yéremy Pino's stirke beats Donnarumma 🎯 pic.twitter.com/5uF4vzOXDp

Whatever hope that mustered was snatched away again when Cherki scored his second goal and the third goal of a breathless five minutes.

His shot at the end of a darting run flicked the ankle of Tomiyasu to send it just out of Henderson’s reach.

Rayan Cherki AGAIN! Manchester City have breathing room once again after another strike from the Frenchman 👏 pic.twitter.com/Tyw9whPS2r

Morocco teenager Ayyoub Bouaddi had little time to show why City have paid Lille £85.6m for him with a late entry as a substitute, but they didn’t need him on this occasion.

Foden then set off on a swerving run that set up Haaland to lash home his second goal of the game and make it 4-1.

Erling Haaland scores gets another! 🔥 pic.twitter.com/4mz2eF7wFF

The fear for Palace is that they cannot keep selling their best players and expecting to replicate the success on the pitch that has brought them three trophies in the past 15 months.

Leicester City offer a shuddering example of that. From Premier League champions to League One in 10 seasons.

Pierre Sage, the new Palace manager, will welcome the certainty that the closure of the transfer window will bring, particularly over the futures of forwards Ismaïla Sarr and Jean-Philippe Mateta, as well as wing-back Daniel Muñoz.

The one player he cannot afford to lose is Wharton, who matched the City midfield on his own at times in the first half.

Sage said: “I think the score is heavy. We stayed in the game for 65 minutes and created some chances. We know we are in for a tough season, but we have created a lot of opportunities in the first two games.

“I could speak about the transfer window, but I don’t want to find an excuse. We just have to be sure that in four days’ time, the team will be better than today.”

We played well, it is a new manager but we have been playing together, with the addition of a few new players. We know what to do and have to trust the system.”

“We have to keep on playing together, find out where we are best and how to play. We have so many good players and we have to fit everyone in. He has to keep going because we know how good Phil is, it is about showing it week in week out. This is the right step forward for everyone. We have to build on this.”

A late double substitution for Manchester City as Reis and Braithwaite come on. Enzo Maresca’s side are cruising to victory to make it two wins from two.

Cherki has two goals to his name and now Haaland does as Manchester City are romping to victory in south London. Guehi wins possession for City inside the Palace half and the ball comes to Foden, who dribbles towards the Palace penalty area. He lays it off to his left to Haaland who, from a narrow angle, finds the root of the net.

Erling Haaland scores gets another! 🔥 pic.twitter.com/4mz2eF7wFF

Nearly an instant impact from McAidoo as the 18-year-old drives through the Palace half and curls a shot from the edge of the box that goes just wide.

When Manchester City were making those substitutions, the Crystal Palace fans were making sure they let the officials know how long the Manchester City players were taking to get off.

There is going to be a debut for the Premier League’s most expensive teenager ever as Bouaddi comes on for Manchester City. McAidoo is also coming on, with Cherki and Anderson going off.

Mingueza eventually comes on but not after having to wait until the ball goes out of play again as Khalaili was adjudged to have taken too long to have got off the pitch. Safe to say the Palace fans are not too impressed with that new rule. It will probably be a pub question in the years ahead. That change does mean that Palace have used all five substitutions, which means Munoz will not come on. He is being linked with a reunion with Oliver Glasner at Nottingham Forest in the final days of this window.

Crystal Palace make another double change and it will be two debuts as Disasi and Mingueza come on.

Enzo Maresca turns to his bench for the first time tonight as Kovacic comes on.

Khalaili brings down Semenyo and is booked for that challenge.

Palace are going to make a double substitution as McNeil and Gozo replace Nketiah and Pino. 19-year-old Gozo is on for his Palace debut.

That was a chance for Palace. Guessand finds Pino, who drives into the Manchester City penalty area on the right. Pino has Nketiah at the far post but there is too much on the cross.

Guessand, back at Palace, is going to come on to replace Strand Larsen, who has been pretty quiet up top for the home side tonight.

Sometimes you feel blessed to witness an extraordinary moment of footballing genius. Selhurst Park has just seen two in the space of three minutes. Yeremy Pino’s free-kick which flicked off the back of Gianluigi Donnarumma was stunning, but even that could not truly compare to the slalom run of Rayan Cherki that drew a collective intake of breath from all those present. The Frenchman has just followed it with a scorching shot. It couldn’t compare with his first, though.

Three goals come in quick succession and Cherki restores Manchester City’s two-goal advantage with his second of the night. The Frenchman receives it on the turn from around 30 yards out and drives towards the Palace penalty area. He then shoots and a kind deflection off Richards takes it over Henderson’s diving effort and into the Palace net.

Rayan Cherki AGAIN! Manchester City have breathing room once again after another strike from the Frenchman 👏 pic.twitter.com/Tyw9whPS2r

Just as the hosts appeared to maybe out of this one, they get a goal back. Pino’s fantastic free-kick strikes the bar, hits Donnarumma on the back before going into the net off the post. That hit the frame of the goal twice and Palace have a crucial goal, minutes after going 2-0 down.

"This is a good a free-kick as you're likely to see this season!" Yéremy Pino's stirke beats Donnarumma 🎯 pic.twitter.com/5uF4vzOXDp

Anderson brings down Pino not far outside the Manchester City penalty area and is booked.

The next goal in this game felt crucial and the visitors have it. Foden drives towards the Palace penalty area before playing a pass forward into the path of Cherki. The Frenchman has numerous defenders around but he shows neat footwork to skip past a few, holds off Richards before slotting home with his left foot.

"The man with the magic feet!"Rayan Cherki doubles Manchester City's lead with a STUNNING goal 😮‍💨 pic.twitter.com/9Zea5vFljv

No-one has had fewer touches on the pitch tonight than Haaland up until this point but the Norwegian’s goal is the difference. His number of touches (14) is the joint fewest with his compatriot Strand Larsen.

That was a good chance for Nketiah. He plays the ball to the underlapping Mitchell, who from the byline cuts it back into the path of Nketiah. The former Arsenal man should so so much better with his opportunity from the edge of the six-yard box but fires a long way wide.

Semenyo wins Manchester City an early corner in this second half off Canvot. Anderson’s delivery beyond the back post picks out O’Reilly, who in space heads back across goal but Pino heads away.

We are back under way at Selhurst Park, with Manchester City carrying a 1-0 lead into this second half. As the players emerged from the tunnels for the second half, the DJ at Selhurst Park paid tribute to the late Dolly Parton and Kenny Rogers by playing Islands in the Stream. Nice touch! Get your favourite Dolly and Kenny tunes in the comments section at the bottom of the blog.

Possession: Crystal Palace 33%-67% Manchester CityShots: 7-11Shots on target: 1-6Corners: 2-2Touches in the opposition box: 10-18

The stats are certainly in Manchester City’s favour and they will feel they probably should have more than the one goal.

Cherki has a late chance for Manchester City but his shot is well saved by Henderson down to his right.

The first half at Selhurst Park is then brought to an end and Manchester City lead 1-0 at the break thanks to Haaland’s header.

There will be just one added minute at the end of this first half.

Palace started off with a nominal back three. That has become a back five far too often for Pierre Sage’s liking at times in this first half, yet still City are playing through them almost at will. The Palace fans whose deafening support accompanied Palace shots in the opening minutes are reduced to cheering battling midfield runs that win a free-kick now.

Pino delivers a free-kick into the Manchester City box and Richards gets to it first. It comes off his shoulder and rolls into the arms of Donnarumma.

Semenyo’s shot from the left side of the box takes a deflection off Richards, forcing Henderson into a decent save.

Palace now miss a big opportunity and should be on level terms. Wharton, who has probably been the best player on the pitch tonight, whips in a cross from the right and picks out Mitchell, who has a free header from eight yards out but somehow misses the target.

Strand Larsen comes close with a header from a Pino cross but he would have been offside anyway.

The first booking of the night goes the way of the visitors. Wharton drives forward into the Manchester City half and is cynically brought down by Cherki, who looked perplexed when the yellow card was shown but it was an obvious booking.

Foden wastes his second big chance of this first half. Manchester City break through O’Reilly, who carries it down the right. He waits for Cherki to make the overlapping run before passing to the Frenchman. Cherki’s cross picks out Foden inside the six-yard box and the latter should score but he gets a simple header all wrong.

Well, that was easy. So easy in fact – perfect Semenyo cross, perfect Haaland header - that it hushed Selhurst Park as the ball looped over Dean Henderson. Even the roar from the enclave of City fans took a moment to fill the south London air. You wouldn’t say that all the pre-match optimism among Palace fans has been punctured, but the home side need a moment if they aren’t to sink without trace to a City side bossing possession and territory now.

That is a huge miss from Foden. Anderson picks out his compatriot in acres of space on the right side of the box, with no Palace defender within five yards of him, but Foden blazes over the bar when he should have put Manchester City 2-0 up.

King Harald V of Norway has died in the last few days and over the last few hours two Norwegian cyclists claimed a one-two at the Vuelta a Espana and now Haaland has a goal.

He has barely touched the ball thus far but he puts the visitors ahead just past the quarter-of-an-hour mark. Semenyo is afforded too much space on the left just outside the penalty area and clips in a cross towards the far post. Haaland gets up highest, above Richards, and guides a superb header over Henderson into the Palace net.

Erling Haaland gets off the mark for the new Premier League season! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/5ZjQUVk6Zl

The England boss is in attendance tonight, perhaps keeping a close eye on that midfield battle between Anderson and Wharton.

Palace flirt with danger inside their own penalty area. After Haaland’s flick, Kamada should just belt the ball away but instead inexplicably leaves it. Henderson manages to mop up just as Foden was eyeing up the chance.

There is a mad scramble inside the Palace box but somehow the hosts escape without conceding. Initially, Anderson’s shot from range is saved by Henderson but Manchester City keep it alive in the penalty area. Palace frantically attempt to clear their lines and eventually they do after Haaland came close.

Quite a lot of the focus tonight will be on two English midfielders; one who has got a big-money move this summer and the other thus far has not. Anderson is directly up against Wharton and so far it is the latter who is winning the early battles, including dispossessing Anderson in midfield.

The first chance of the game goes the way of the hosts. It stems from a quite sensational first-time pass from Wharton from inside his own half into the left channel to pick out the run of Nketiah, whose shot from the left side of the box takes a deflection off Dias and is saved by Donnarumma.

Manchester City initially clear the corner but Palace keep it alive. Kamada’s shot from just inside the box appeared to be on target but it is headed over for another corner, which is easily caught by Donnarumma.

We are under way at Selhurst Park. Will Pierre Sage earn his first win as Palace boss or can Enzo Maresca and City make it two wins from two?

Both sides emerge from the tunnel in the corner of Selhurst Park to the customary sound of Glad All Over and we are moments away from kick-off in south London. Here is a reminder of how the two sides line up this evening:

Crystal Palace: Henderson, Khalaili, Canvot, Richards, Tomiyasu, Mitchell, Wharton, Kamada, Pino, Strand Larsen, Nketiah.Substitutes: Benitez, Munoz, Disasi, Mingueza, Hughes, Lerma, Gozo, McNeil, Guessand.

Manchester City: Donnarumma, Khusanov, Dias, Gvardiol, O’Reilly, Anderson, Guehi, Cherki, Foden Semenyo, Haaland.Substitutes: Rulli, Kovacic, Ait-Nouri, Reis, Echeverri, Bouaddi, McAidoo, Braithwaite, Lewis.

Yes! It may have been fleeting but the boy in the Palace tracksuit top had his moment after all with Erling Haaland as City waited in line to enter the Selhurst Park pitch. And having done so, he fairly skipped up the steps back with his dad back to their seats. Whether the boy’s second wish of the evening, for a Palace victory, will come true is another question altogether.

The young Palace fan is still waiting for Haaland. Another determined walk back to the dressing room. It isn’t a simple task to attract an opposition player’s attention when you are leaning over a barrier a few feet higher than him – and in the home end. Haaland and his teammates have the look of a team that knows it must perform tonight to ease the concerns that they are a team in transition. The City fans will not entertain such thoughts, either.

Crystal Palace looked set to sign Club Brugge defender Joel Ordonez but that deal could be in doubt as there may be some problems with his medical. We await to see further updates on that situation.

“He is a genius. Make no mistake. Managers now want structure, they do not like players who are a bit loose out of possession. But I go to football matches to watch people like him play.

“That is what makes me smile. I do not like watching players pass it sideways, that is not why I go to football. I go to watch geniuses do their work. Some managers will not appreciate it. But last week he got his manager out of a hole because without him they would not have won that game.”

"He's irreplaceable" 💥Jamie Redknapp and Clinton Morrison sing the praises of Crystal Palace's Adam Wharton 🤝 pic.twitter.com/ZOpcZcItHY

Jack Grealish is not in the Manchester City squad tonight amid links with the likes of Everton and Sunderland. Will he still be at the club beyond the deadline? It would appear not.

Both Ismaila Sarr and Jean-Philippe Mateta are out of the Crystal Palace squad tonight with injury but could they be on the move before the window slams shut? Sarr has been linked with Galatasaray and Liverpool whilst the situation is complicated with Mateta as he claims the final year of his contract is void. How do those two situations resolve themselves? Daniel Munoz has been linked with a move to Nottingham Forest but is on the bench for Palace this evening.

An unfulfilled wish so far for a young Palace fan holding up a child’s red Norway shirt with ‘Haaland’ emblazoned on it. Having waited patiently for the City players to emerge for their warm-up and being held by his dad as he leant over the stone wall to attract Haaland’s attention, he was left disappointed because the City striker was simply not looking as he and his teammates jogged past. Will the boy, who has on a Palace tracksuit top, get a photo with his hero when the striker returns to the Portakabin that hosts the away dressing room prior to kick-off? Stay tuned.

"The results will certainly come" ✅Dean Henderson urges patience as Crystal Palace go through a transitional period under new manager Pierre Sage 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/1pJjRPeKko

"On the ball I think he's very good, off the ball he's strong" Enzo Maresca explains why he played Marc Guéhi in midfield in Manchester City's opening game against Bournemouth 🤔 pic.twitter.com/h4N1e1L8bf

"At home anything is possible" 💪Pierre Sage previews his sides clash with Manchester City at Selhurst Park 🔥 pic.twitter.com/oPJnZJVB6B

"He'll be very vital for us" 🔑Nico O'Reilly speaking about Manchester City's new signing Ayyoub Bouaddi ahead of their game against Crystal Palace 🔊 pic.twitter.com/2ptihsCY7c

Crystal Palace: Henderson, Khalaili, Canvot, Richards, Tomiyasu, Mitchell, Wharton, Kamada, Pino, Strand Larsen, Nketiah.Substitutes: Benitez, Munoz, Disasi, Mingueza, Hughes, Lerma, Gozo, McNeil, Guessand.

There looks set to be a debut for the Premier League’s most expensive teenager off the visitors’ bench in the form of Ayyoub Bouaddi. There is no Jack Grealish in their squad as his future is up in the air.

Manchester City: Donnarumma, Khusanov, Dias, Gvardiol, O’Reilly, Anderson, Guehi, Cherki, Foden Semenyo, Haaland.Substitutes: Rulli, Kovacic, Ait-Nouri, Reis, Echeverri, Bouaddi, McAidoo, Braithwaite, Lewis.

Was it really just a year ago when Crystal Palace fans flooded down the Holmesdale Road with not a care in the world having just won the Community Shield to add to their FA Cup triumph over tonight’s opponents Manchester City? Well, they are marching along the Holmesdale Road in the same numbers again this evening, bedecked in red and blue as always, yet there is uncertainty and worry in the air and on their faces. Will the player exodus continue? What should they make of new manager Pierre Sage? Will the good times fade from view as quickly as they did for Leicester City or can Sage build a new side to match the one which, under Oliver Glasner, added the Conference League to their list of trophies three months ago?

“We struggled to get into the game and win the battles,” a disappointed Carlo Ancelotti lamented.

At the World Cup, an industrious 18-year-old showed maturity beyond his years to dominate the midfield against Ancelotti’s Brazil on his competitive international debut, earning Morocco a draw. That was, in fact, the second time an Ancelotti side had been undone by precocious teenager Ayyoub Bouaddi.

Ancelotti’s remarks about losing the midfield battle are from after a Champions League match in October 2024, when Lille shocked Real Madrid to end their 36-game unbeaten run. Bouaddi was at the heart of both statement results for his club and country.

Tonight's team to face Crystal Palace! ​​💪🩵XI | Donnarumma, Khusanov, Dias (C), Gvardiol, O'Reilly, Anderson, Guéhi, Foden, Cherki, Semenyo, HaalandSUBS | Rulli, Kovačić, Aït-Nouri, Reis, Echeverri, Bouaddi, McAidoo, Braithwaite, Lewis🤝 @etihad pic.twitter.com/qNgJPXKDM7

The second weekend of the Premier League season kicks off under the lights in South London as Crystal Palace host Manchester City at Selhurst Park. Manchester City won both fixtures 3-0 last season and they are in fact unbeaten in their last 11 Premier league away games against Crystal Palace, who have won just two of the 22 top flight meetings.

Crystal Palace experienced defeat on the opening weekend, falling to a 2-0 loss at Everton last Saturday, meaning the Pierre Sage era started with a defeat. Tonight is Sage’s first home game in charge of the club.

“I think it will be a wonderful moment, but I prefer to have a wonderful moment with good news at the end of the game,” Sage said. “That is why I do not think about me in this situation. The most important thing is the team and the result for sure, because we prepare all the week for that, to make them [the fans] happy. They will be happy to see us, but I think they would prefer to see us win. I will give my life to make them happy. I cannot do more. When you are in this stadium [Selhurst Park], you feel the history. You feel that there is something heavy weighing on you. It is a great responsibility that I have been entrusted with. We cannot wait to see this stadium in action.”

Sage has confirmed that Ismaila Sarr, who has been linked with a move away from the club this summer, and Chadi Riad will miss out tonight due to injury, as will striker Jean-Philippe Mateta. Palace have confirmed the addition of Axel Disasi on loan from Chelsea and the French defender could be involved tonight.

Manchester City appeared to be heading towards defeat in Enzo Maresca’s first league game in charge of the club last weekend. They were 1-0 down at home against Bournemouth in the closing stages before goals from Marc Guehi and Josko Gvardiol gave them a come-from-behind win.

It has been a busy week in the transfer window for Manchester City. Both Savio (formerly Savinho) and Omar Marmoush have left for Tottenham, joining a long list of departures from the Etihad this summer. Moroccan midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi has arrived in an £85m deal from Lille and has become the most expensive teenager in Premier League history. Maresca has confirmed that 18-year-old Bouaddi is ready to start.

“He [Bouaddi] is ready,” Maresca said. “He was working with his former club so he is fit. We will see how long he needs in terms of adaptation but he is ready to go. He is quite calm. He does not look 18, he already looks older, which is important. But in this case, we need to go slowly because he is very young, he has come from a different country so there is no rush for him. He is going to help us now and in the future. He is very mature for being 18.”

Team news from Selhurst Park to follow shortly.

#2230. Gary Neville and Jamie Redknapp tear into Man Utd after Tottenham draw

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United have come under fresh criticism after their disappointing 1-1 draw with Tottenham Hotspur, with Sky Sports pundits Gary Neville and Jamie Redknapp questioning the team’s performance and the challenges facing Michael Carrick.

Manchester United looked on course for a much-needed victory at Old Trafford after Bryan Mbeumo put them ahead in the second half. However, despite Tottenham being reduced to 10 men, Dominic Solanke’s late equaliser denied Carrick’s side all three points.

Gary Neville felt Tottenham deserved the points, pointing to Solanke’s late goal and his impact as Tottenham captain.

“Tottenham deserved a point. That was a really important moment for Solanke. He’d missed some big chances and was captain for the first time,” Neville said on Sky Sports.

“They were the better team by far. If they’d left without a point, it would have been terrible for them.”

The former United defender also expressed concern about what the result means for Carrick, who faces increasing pressure to improve performances and results.

“Michael Carrick is left with a lot to think about. It was a worrying day in terms of the level of performance and a big week ahead.”

Manchester United spent massively in the summer to overhaul their midfield. However, Jamie Redknapp was critical of the performance he saw on the pitch.

“I do not see enough connections in that midfield, and they look devoid of any confidence, ideas, or patterns of play, playing out the back,” Redknapp said.

“Tottenham were just much better than them in every department, but that is a theme this season.”

The former Liverpool midfielder also questioned United’s energy and attacking organization, suggesting the squad is not strong enough to meet the demands placed upon it.

“Their energy levels are not good enough, and they look loose going forward; there was no real structure.”

Redknapp added that Carrick cannot fix every issue alone, insisting the manager needs backing to improve the squad.

“The squad is not good or strong enough, and Michael [Carrick] needs help in that respect.”

#2228. ‘Embarrassing themselves!’ Jamie Carragher hits back at Rio Ferdinand over Cristiano Ronaldo defence

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Jamie Carragher has taken aim at Rio Ferdinand for defending Cristiano Ronaldo following the Portuguese forward’s latest controversy with his national team.

Ronaldo has found himself at the centre of a growing dispute after abruptly leaving Portugal’s national team camp following a reported disagreement with head coach Jorge Jesus. The incident has prompted strong reactions from former teammates and pundits, with Ferdinand firmly siding with the Al-Nassr star.

Jamie Carragher, however, believes Ronaldo’s reputation should not shield him from criticism when his behaviour becomes difficult to defend.

Rio Ferdinand, who played alongside Cristiano Ronaldo at Manchester United between 2003 and 2009, criticised Jorge Jesus for the way he handled the situation.

Speaking on his Rio Presents podcast, the former United captain criticised Jesus for not showing respect to Cristiano Ronaldo.

“Cristiano Ronaldo was put in a very bad situation and was treated in an inappropriate way. He has an enormous history in football. Jorge Jesus did not deal with Ronaldo well and chose to treat him in that way, but I cannot find any explanation for it,” Ferdinand said.

Despite Jesus being Portugal’s manager, Ferdinand questioned his standing, comparing him with the likes of Sir Alex Ferguson and Pep Guardiola. To say the least, Ferdinand only embarrassed himself doing that.

Jamie Carragher saw the argument very differently and rightfully so.

Speaking on The Overlap Daily, the former Liverpool defender suggested that Ferdinand’s friendship with Ronaldo was influencing his reaction to the incident.

“People think it’s good to be close to people in the game, but this is where it becomes a problem,” Carragher explained.

He then called out both Ferdinand and broadcaster Piers Morgan, who has also been vocal in his support of Ronaldo.

“People like Piers Morgan and Rio Ferdinand, who are big people in the media whether you like them or not, are embarrassing themselves with the nonsense that they’re coming out with because they know Ronaldo. You can know someone and try to look after them, but you cannot defend the indefensible.”

Carragher believes Ronaldo’s achievements should not put the forward beyond criticism, particularly when his actions involve his national team and its management.

Gary Neville, who also played with Cristiano Ronaldo, has questioned Ronaldo’s handling of the situation, despite his longstanding affection for his former Manchester United teammate.

Neville argued that Ronaldo’s public response had made matters worse and the forward needed to accept criticism rather than expect others to defend him.

“With Cristiano, it’s difficult because I love him, but I can’t watch what happened at United in his second period and then see him make a statement like that without saying something. He has to be pulled up on that and told that it isn’t acceptable,” Neville said.

He also suggested Ronaldo’s extraordinary success, wealth and influence could have contributed to a sense that he was beyond challenge.

“When you have a billion pounds in the bank, the achievements he has had and the power he has, you feel you’re unbreakable, you feel you’re unstoppable,” Neville added.

Despite his criticism, Neville does not believe the episode will define Ronaldo’s legacy permanently. He expects the attention to fade once the forward retires, allowing his achievements on the pitch to take centre stage again.

#2227. ‘Upset’ - Ryan Alebiosu sends message to Blackburn Rovers fans after suffering new blow

Blackburn Rovers star Ryan Alebiosu has seemingly confirmed that he will not be available for selection again until 2027.

The athletic right-back limped off during the first half of Rovers' 2-1 loss to Stoke City in midweek, as he managed just 40 minutes before being forced out of the game with an issue.

The 24-year-old has been a key figure for the Lancashire outfit so far this campaign, featuring in all of their opening 14 league matches.

So his absence will come as a big blow for Tony Mowbray, who will have to handle missing one of their top stars for the remainder of the calendar year.

Summer signing Gady Beyuku was brought on to replace Alebiosu late in the first half, with the team going 1-0 down just a few moments later, with the Potters sealing all three points in the second half.

Alebiosu has confirmed on his Instagram page that he will be absent for the remainder of 2026, ruling him out for a number of weeks with an issue.

The defender was initially a doubt for this weekend’s clash against West Ham, with Mowbray hopeful he could be available, but a further scan has revealed a more significant issue than first feared.

“Gutted, upset but god has bigger plans,” wrote Alebiosu.

“Will be back stronger for sure, see you 2027 Rovers.”

Alebiosu also missed a period of games for Blackburn last season due to the Africa Cup of Nations, but his absence will still be a big blow for the team.

The defender has previously been linked with the likes of Everton off the back of his performances at Ewood Park, following a 2025 move from Belgian outfit Kortrijk.

This injury also means he will miss the upcoming Lancashire derby against bitter rivals Burnley, which will be a particularly painful pill for Mowbray to swallow.

No exact timeframe has been given for his potential return beyond 2027, meaning he will be absent for at least eight weeks.

Alebiosu had started each of Rovers’ first 14 league fixtures, and he’s been one of the standout performers under Mowbray so far this term.

The full-back has impressed going forward, completing 0.85 dribbles per 90, and getting 1.85 touches in the opposition area each game on average (all stats from Fotmob).

He contributed one goal and five assists from 39 appearances in the Championship last season, highlighting his attacking threat, although he is yet to register either a goal or assist in 2026/27.

Alebiosu’s absence is a massive blow for Mowbray, as he has become a very dependable performer for the club.

And with a more inexperienced figure in Beyuku coming in for the Nigerian - one who hasn't necessarily impressed in his cameos so far - there may be some short-term pain at Ewood Park whilst the French defender gets to grips with the Championship.

How big of an absence will Ryan Alebiosu be for Blackburn? Comment your opinion below

The 20-year-old only has four substitute appearances to his name at this stage, having arrived in the summer, and Mowbray may want to find another solution than putting him straight into the starting lineup.

An injury of around eight weeks means that the experienced coach will have to get creative to deal with this particular injury issue.

#2225. Is Mainoo-Tielemans the right midfield option for Man Utd?

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United drew 1-1 at home to Tottenham despite having an extra man advantage. The Reds saw Mbeumo put them in front, but Solanke scored a late leveller in injury time after Bentancur was shown a red card for headbutting Luke Shaw.

Manchester United’s worrisome season continues after accumulating just six points off the first six games, their first start in 40 years. But more than the results, what worries Manchester United is their midfield pairing.

United spent massively on their midfield rebuild and somehow can’t find the best combination in the midfield. Michael Carrick has gone with the Mainoo-Tielemans partnership, but they have failed to control the midfield. Individually, they both come with decent numbers, but collectively they fall short.

Mainoo and Tielemans struggled against Tottenham while closing the midfield and at times showed a lack of energy. On the day when nothing clicked for United, the Mainoo-Tielemans partnership particularly raised eyebrows.

Gary Neville has also raised serious concerns about Manchester United’s Mainoo-Tielemans partnership.

Neville was particularly unimpressed by the midfield balance, arguing that the problems went beyond one disappointing performance.

The former United captain stopped short of ruling out the combination altogether, but he suggested he has serious doubts about its suitability.

“Tielemans and Mainoo, I’m not calling time on it, that’s probably too drastic, but I’ve seen enough of it to think that’s not a midfield that’s dynamic enough to play at this football club in the Premier League.”

Former Spurs midfielder Redknapp felt United struggled to connect their midfield with the rest of the team during the opening stages.

He added: “I didn’t see enough connections in that midfield in the first hour. Baleba came on and did OK and showed a bit more.

“They look devoid of any confidence, any idea, any patterns of play, playing out from the back. Tottenham were much better than them in every single department.”

While Carlos Baleba was a particular highlight on the day, he showed great potential when brought on. He brought a new sense of energy in the midfield and sent a few balls over the top for a couple of quick counterattacks as well.

Redknapp also pointed to the physical demands of modern Premier League football, arguing that United cannot afford to be outworked by their opponents.

Tottenham ran a staggering 5 km more than Manchester United, something Redknapp felt was a pattern.

"Spurs ran 5km more than Man United… it's like that EVERY GAME!"Jamie Redknapp is less than impressed with the lack of ground covered this season by Manchester United 😬 pic.twitter.com/BxWkFuyGJ1

“There is a pattern that I don’t really like when I watch teams, and that’s when every time the stats don’t lie and the other team runs more than you.

“I feel in Premier League football right now there are a couple of non-negotiables, and one is you have to run more than the other team if you want to win or at least get close enough. Tonight Spurs ran 5km more than Manchester United.”

He believes Tottenham’s pressing exposed the lack of pace in United’s midfield, making it difficult for the hosts to move the ball safely through the centre.

“In terms of how they played today, I think they have an issue with Tielemans and Mainoo in midfield. I don’t see enough energy in there. Baleba will add a lot and will give them a tremendous amount of energy but right now, when things aren’t going well… and Tottenham knew it!

“Every time United played the ball out from the back they pounced. They pressed them because they knew United don’t have the pace and speed in midfield to get away.”

“In isolation, one of them is absolutely fine, the two of them together doesn’t work for me. They haven’t got the pace or the energy to get around the pitch for 90 minutes.”
