#2136. ‘Hello darkness my old friend, soon you’ll be here by 5pm’ As Simon and Garfunkel never sang…

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Back in August I contributed an article to The Mag which was entitled “The Phoney War”, it was about the lull before hostilities began at the start of the Newcastle United season.

In September I contributed “All Things Bright and Beautiful”, about our promising start to the season.

October’s article “Trick or Treat” arrived a little late last weekend. It raised doubts about how things are unfolding after a series of sloppy defeats.

My offering this month? Fire and darkness.

November starts with the dispiriting onset of darkness. As Simon and Garfunkel never sang, “Hello darkness my old friend, soon you’ll be here by 5pm.”

Darkness aside, there’s been more futility than fire from our footballing favourites. Maybe we’ll see a spark from Newcastle United in West London on Saturday.

Maybe we’ll see two bald men fighting over a comb. An increasingly dull, dreary and desperate attempt to win the coveted prize of being the fourth worst team in the league by the end of the season.

There’s always hope, of course, the thing that kills you.

We hope that Fulham will be even more wobbly than us. We hope that we can bag a fourth win of a mercurial season in the capital this weekend. We hope that the likes of Sunderland, Coventry, Ipswich, Palace, Fulham will finish below us by the odd point or with a less embarrassing goal difference. We hope that Santa will bring us a little stocking filler in the form of a relegation berth for Man City. If so, we hope that we won’t be one of the other two trapdoor teams. We hope that it’s going to be alright. We hope Matthias Jaissle will turn it around. We hope that the Newcastle United players will get it. We hope there’s something for them to get. We hope for a couple of signings in January. We know all about hope as Newcastle supporters. We know the sorts of things we say in our brighter moments. But November darkness doesn’t encourage hope.

There’s a beguiling song by an obscure folk singer Dave Goulder, entitled “The January Man”. It’s partly about the changing seasons, month by month. This month’s line is, “The poor November man sees fire and wind and mist and rain and winter air.” We can identify with that. So can our current manager, who looked like the poor November man at the end of Monday night’s match after shaking hands with the gargoyle Moyes.

If you want a giggle in November’s darkness, search up “David Moyes Dunfermline”. It should bring up an image of a Soccer Stars/Panini type sticker of a young Davey Moyes in his playing days. Be warned: it belongs on the Halloween clearance shelf. Unsettling. NSFW.

We might giggle but fly old Davey has demonstrated a certain brand of English football to MJ three times these last few months. As my Mam used to say, “that’ll learn him a thing or three.”

Aggregate score 7-2. Gesundheit, or something that rhymes with it.

Despite the hype of the Premier League being the world’s finest, we all know the reality: there’s an awful lot of beige football. Much of what is served up is tepid soup prepared by chefs like Moyes, using ingredients from the back of the fridge and the darkest corners of the cupboards. It sustains life but does not bring joy.

Welcome to Richard Masters’ soup kitchen. One bit of bread to dunk each, except for the slippery six. They’re on the “all you can eat” tariff, butter running down their greasy chins. No soup for them. They’re having steak, followed by a selection from the sweet trolley. Coffee. Brandy and cigars.

Here’s the recipe for Masters’ Beige Football Soup, a tried and trusted staple of the English football diet.

The main ingredients: – a pound of Pulis – five fat Sam fingers – a whiffling of Warnock’s whiskers – a measure of Moysie’s mustard – a handful of Hughes hoofball – a brace of Bruceballs. Lob in a few streaky rashers and a head of cabbage.

Method: Clag it all into a pan on a low heat until tepid.

Before serving, add the following to taste: – a dash of well-drilled defence – a rasher of rogue refereeing – a pinch of percentages – a layer of long-throw – a jar of “Wee Davey’s” jam – a measure of Monday night marinade – a can of barely concealed corruption – a scoop of Stoke soil, ideally harvested on a cold, wet midweek night.

Enough nutritional content and calories to keep you up. Best served lukewarm from a vat of vested interests into leaking, cracked bowls, just enough to accumulate points.

November: the month of fire and darkness. Maybe Matthias Jaissle can kindle fire in the hearts of our lads and us supporters. Maybe there’ll be a light in the darkness on Saturday.

#2135. St Mirren sick of Old Firm 'hard luck' stories as Rangers come calling

Craig McLeish does not want the Old Firm to be a “hard luck story” for St Mirren as he prepares for the visit of Rangers in the William Hill Premiership on Saturday night.

Since moving from the youth set-up to become Buddies boss in March – initially on a temporary basis before making the move permanent in June – McLeish’s side have run both Celtic and Rangers close on several occasions.

Most recently, St Mirren lost to a last-gasp goal in a 1-0 defeat at Ibrox, following a 2-1 home defeat to Celtic and a 5-1 defeat away to Rangers in the Premier Sports Cup.

In his dugout debut for Saints in March, Rangers won 1-0 in Paisley, before St Mirren went down 1-0 at Celtic Park before taking the Hoops to extra-time in the Scottish Cup semi-final, only to eventually lose 6-2.

McLeish said: “We don’t want to be the hard luck story every time we play against them and you get plaudits like, ‘oh well done you played well but unlucky again’.

“We want to be able to go toe-to-toe with anyone in the league and come out with positive results and against Rangers and Celtic, we have not managed to do that.

“A couple of the games have got away from us and that’s what you’re trying to fight against and make sure that the games do go right to the end and you’re always in with a chance.

“That’s the bit now for us as a group and confidence within the group, to go and get a positive result against one of them – that’s probably the next step for us.

“We’ve had a look at Rangers twice (this season) as well, and we obviously have to change some bits just because of personnel available to us.

“You’re just trying to constantly learn and adapt from the games that you’re playing against teams.

“You have to take those experiences on and just tweak little bits to it, so there will be little bits that we try and throw at Rangers that they’ve not seen from us before as well.

“That’s what we have to try to do. We have to try and be unpredictable with it.”

#2134. Sullivan Sidelined As West Ham’s Parker Decision Revealed

Claret & Hugh can reveal today that, despite reports to the contrary, David Sullivan had no input into the decision to appoint Scott Parker as West Ham United’s new manager.

Some reports in the national media have suggested that Sullivan reacted to the Hammers’ back-to-back defeats against Southampton and West Bromwich Albion by convincing the board to sack Nuno Espírito Santo and appoint Parker. However, information received by C&H indicates that this was not the case.

Instead, we understand that the decision was driven by West Ham chief executive Karim Virani, who, following meetings on Monday, approached the board for permission to dismiss Nuno and appoint Parker. The former Hammers midfielder was already the preferred candidate, with one club insider describing him to us today as “the perfect fit”.

And it has very much been Virani liaising with Daniel Kretinsky which has prompted the club to change direction so quickly.

Karim Virani was the driving force behind the appointment of Scott Parker

The concern surrounding Nuno’s position had been building for some time and was not simply a reaction to two disappointing results. There was growing dissatisfaction within the club over performances across a number of matches, with the defeat to West Bromwich Albion effectively proving to be the last straw.

Virani subsequently decided to act more quickly than originally anticipated, with performances showing no sign of improvement. As Claret & Hugh revealed earlier this week, Monday’s meeting brought forward a dismissal which had initially been expected to come after further consideration.

Parker was very much at the top of the list, and Virani sought the board’s approval to proceed with the change. Our latest information makes an important distinction between the board approving the appointment and Sullivan personally driving the decision.

Far from being a Sullivan-led intervention following the Southampton and West Brom defeats, C&H understands that it was Virani who took the initiative to end Nuno’s tenure and bring Parker back to West Ham.

Kris Gonzo (commonly known to the West Ham community as Gonzo) is the co-founder of Hammers Chat (established 2014) and the lead video content creator and columnist for Claret and Hugh.

With over a decade of professional sports media experience, he is a frequent West Ham United analyst and contributor for Sky Sports News, BBC Football Focus, and BBC Radio 5 Live. He previously served as an official video and content creator for West Ham United FC during the club's tenure at Upton Park and featured in the official documentary commemorating the historic final game at the Boleyn Ground.

A lifelong Hammer since the legendary 10-0 victory over Bury, when he isn't providing daily match analysis on the Hammers Chat YouTube Channel or broadcasting on X (@GONZObignose), he can be found walking his dog and restoring classic pinball machines.

Of course Sullivan would like people to think he’s not involved and not making the decisions. Then he gets off Scot free doesn’t he.

Can’t believe that a chief executive Virani is now the man making the decisions about sacking a manager. How have we got into a position where we have owners that are not personally driving what happens in their own club. Soon as Sullivan and Kretinsky get out of our club the better.

I heard that David Sullivan had advised Karim to make this change now.

We have already read all about how Sullivan resigned from the board of West Ham the football club, he doesn’t have any operational say!

He is only a board member of holding company, and can override special resolutions.

A majority shareholder has no say in who manages his club/investment whatever your views about Sullivan this is one very bizzare story….

Good. Sideline Sullivan and you’re in with some chance of a sensible and timely decision. The number one aim is to get back to the premier league for financial reasons and Parker has to be your number one choice for attaining that aim. Correct decision at the correct moment, nothing at all like Sullivan. What happens in the premier league is only an issue if you actually get there.

#2132. Hammers outcasts no longer | Training hint suggests a new direction for Scott Parker’s West Ham

Blackburn Rovers await West Ham United tomorrow, with a second long trip within three days. According to local news outlets, the Irons squad is flying to Blackpool Airport this afternoon rather than endure another gruelling coach journey.

After the 450 mile midweek journey to Cardiff, going by road would have meant the West Ham teams’ tired bodies would have faced the even longer 490 mile round trip to Ewood Park – probably five hours each way – hardly the best preparation after minimal recovery.

However, a two week international break beckons during which time Scott Parker can really start to work on his tactics without the irritations of a game to interrupt his progress.

From the Hammers’ PR images released ahead of the Blackburn game, it is clear that this new broom has swept very clean in all corners of the training ground: Several players banished by Nuno are evidently now off the naughty step and, if appearances are anything to go by, are loving life under their new boss.

Maxwel Cornet, the forgotten man under successive managers, evidently got some 1:1 time with his new coach:

Presumably new West Ham manager Scott Parker is pointing out directions to the medical centre

Edson Alvarez, similarly, looks energised and content with his lot which suggests he’s in a better place now that his nemesis Nuno Espírito Santo has departed the training centre.

And one look at Alphonse Areola’s expression says it all. Training has just taken on a new dimension for the French former number three who hasn’t featured in a West Ham side since well before relegation: Parker’s chosen shot stopper at Fulham, remember.

Areola – does that smile reveal that he knows something we don’t for the starting XI tomorrow? We can but hope: I’ll wager that’s a “yes”

After Scott Parkers’ selection of a rusty Soungutou Magassa as a defensive midfielder on Wednesday, the smart money might be on another similar selection involving Magassa or Alvarez tomorrow: That would certainly account for the Mexican’s more upbeat demeanour during the training session and might even please a certain vocal selection of the fan base who have been long advancing the Mexican as the solution to the Hammers’ midfield problems.

#2131. Insider : Massive shift of influence at the heart of West Ham leadership

AWAY from the training pitch and from all things Scott Parker for a second, with a change of focus to events within the board room and at the helm of West Ham United. In the absence of any definitive statement from the club, recent reports had speculated that the Kretinsky – Sullivan pact might be the direction of travel for the season, ahead of a renewed push towards an Amanda Staveley – led takeover next year.

Whatever the long term prognosis or direction of travel, it is clear that there’s a very different Modus Operandi of this West Ham United and the influence of one David Sullivan appears to be, reassuringly, well and truly on the wane.

Kretinsky – fully involved, according to our source, along with the CEO in the behind the scenes running of the football club

Our club insider – speaking on the guarantee of anonymity to protect their position – described earlier the mechanism in place for Scott Parker’s appointment but evidently there’s more shift of management style than perhaps we’d given credit.

“Acting Chief Exec Karim Virani now fully immersed in the day to day running of the club and now liasing with major shareholder Daniel Kretinsky on relevant matters”.

Virani, whilst still ‘acting’ CEO’ by title, appears now very much immersed in the leadership of the club and was, according to Jacob Steinberg, involved along with Nils Koppen in the decision to part company with Nuno Espírito Santo – not before time.

Apparently just two weeks ago CEO Virani flew out to Prague for a meeting with Kretinsky who is, in turn, now apparently ‘fully engaged’ himself in the leadership of the football club and has attended recent games.

Sullivan appears either sidelined, or disinterested, or both.

#2130. ‘I have been a fan so I understand the frustrations…’ Dan Burn

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Dan Burn is back in the Newcastle United team.

After his World Cup adventure this summer, the newly installed captain having to be patient as an ankle injury put him on the NUFC sidelines.

Following brief cameos off the bench in the defeats to Coventry and Aston Villa, Dan Burn was back in the Newcastle United team for the most recent trip to London.

Dan Burn and Fabian Schar replacing Malick Thiaw and Sven Botman, as the pair helped United keep a rare clean sheet and win 2-0 at Selhurst Park.

However, that victory over Crystal Palace then quickly followed a return to doom and gloom with consecutive defeats to Everton in the Carabao Cup and Premier League.

Dan Burn reflecting: “Disappointed, frustrated…the last few games. Between the boxes we do okay but we are not ruthless enough going forward or defending our own box. When you are not winning games there is always a lack of confidence. The fans weren’t happy on Monday night] and they showed that at half-time and full-time. That doesn’t make it easy to build confidence when you are in that atmosphere. But I have been a fan so I understand the frustrations when they are not getting what they’re expecting. That wasn’t a Newcastle performance like we have expected in the last three or four years so I can completely understand the frustrations. It doesn’t make it easier for us as players. You can sense that nervousness in the ground…”

Dan Burn going on to talk about how the performance, the way the Newcastle United team played, didn’t match what had happened on the training ground and the expectations Matthias Jaissle had of the side: “From the first minute to the last minute that wasn’t a performance that he [Matthias Jaissle] expected from us, what we had prepared for, all the work that the staff put in to prepare us for games. A lot of the time, it probably isn’t tactical, it is more of a mentality thing from us. Not winning enough duels, not doing probably the ugly side of the game, which sometimes gives you that little bit of luck to get the game over. There’s probably a lack of confidence at both ends. We sort of feel that towards the end when we are chasing a game and we just need that little bit of decisiveness…but we are snatching at a few bits. I think it is the confidence thing and when it is going well and we have got that good momentum, it just seems to happen and we are not really thinking about it. We are thinking about things too much when going forward and probably not as fluid as we would like to be.”

Asked about adapting to the way Matthias Jaissle wants his Newcastle United team to play, Dan Burn: “I do think we are…but I still think you have to understand we have had a two-week pre-season [with Matthias Jaissle] and we are now three months in, still plenty of time for us to learn and get that. I will say what I have said before, we need stability and unity between us as players, us as a staff and us as a club, to push on and have that us against the world mentality.”

#2129. Derek McInnes delivers 'unbelievable' verdict on unsung Rangers standout

Derek McInnes is happy for goalkeeper Ivor Pandur to stay under the radar at Rangers.

Along with centre-back Owelthu Makhanya, the 26-year-old Croatian goalkeeper has been the Light Blues’ most consistent player this season following his move from Hull City on a four-year deal in the summer.

Pandur has brought a sense of calm to the Gers defence, which was demonstrated again in the 1-0 Premier Sports Cup semi-final win over Aberdeen at Barclays Hampden on Saturday.

Ahead of the William Hill Premiership clash with St Mirren in Paisley on Saturday night, an appreciative McInnes said: “I think he’s done so well.

“The fact I don’t really get asked a lot about Pandur, he’s just so quietly effective, and I think the players hold such a high regard for him and take confidence from him.

“There’s nothing worse — I’ve been there as a player when you’re not sure about your goalie and it affects a lot of what’s happening on the pitch. But when you know you’ve got a good one there, it sends out the exact opposite.

“The confidence that he sends throughout the team I think is clear, whether it’s dealing with things at his feet, in the air.

“His shot-stopping is unbelievable. I watch him in training – every shot has the same importance. He just wants to keep the ball out of his net and, for me, they’re the best types.

“He doesn’t try harder for one shot than he does the next one. Everything is ‘You’re not beating me’, I think he plays the game that way. He’s been brilliant.”

Rangers will face Hibernian in the Premier Sports Cup final next month and McInnes stressed the positives of taking the penultimate step towards the first trophy of the season and of his career as Gers boss.

The former Rangers midfielder said: “It’s been really as you’d expect. I think you’ve got to take the good for the game.

“It’s not easy getting to a cup final, and the fact that we’re there now, you’ve got to try and be pleased with that.

“I think the whole club — I was at the Charity Foundation ball on Sunday — and everybody’s so excited about going to the cup final, and that’s where we should be.

“It should be the norm that we should be feeling that we’re turning up at cup finals and putting ourselves in a position.

“We’ll look forward to it when it comes around, but I think it’s important now that we just really focus on this game before we get into the break, because it can easily dissipate, all that excitement and optimism, on the back of the next result.

“That’s how fickle it is. You’ve got to stay on the job.”

#2128. Fulham v Newcastle United preview ahead of Premier League clash

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Welcome to the Fulham v Newcastle United preview.

Saturday 7th November and a 3pm kick-off.

Newcastle United travel to London this weekend looking to draw a line under a disastrous double defeat in League and Cup to Everton, that has the potential to derail our season before it’s really got started.

The Toon will be hoping to get their season back on track before a tedious international break is followed by a make or break run of fixtures that may very well define the campaign.

Despite this being our thirteenth match of 2026-27, this will be only our second game of the season not selected for live TV. Meaning we can enjoy the comparative luxury of a Saturday 3pm kick-off and travelling Toon fans should have plenty of time to enjoy before and after the match…fingers crossed they’ll enjoy the actual match itself as well!

Newcastle have won two and lost four of their past six league matches as a decent start to the season has disintegrated to an alarming degree. Wins have come against Hull City and Crystal Palace but terrible defeats against four ordinary teams in the shape of Leeds, Coventry, Villa and Everton have seen the Toon drop a very achievable twelve points. We’ve scored six goals in these six matches but conceded a whopping eleven and only kept one clean sheet. The six points gained has us languishing in thirteenth position but a reflection of a bang average league means we could squeeze into the top seven this weekend should all results go our way.

Fulham have won two, drawn three and lost one of their past six league games. Victories have come against Coventry and Hull whilst they’ve drawn with Liverpool, Man United and Aston Villa. Their loss came away at Ipswich. They’ve scored five goals in these games and conceded four. They currently sit fifteenth in the league despite a dreadful start to the season that saw them take just two points from their first six matches. A win at the weekend would see them leapfrog the Toon and could see them as high as eighth depending on results elsewhere.

Newcastle hosted Everton on Monday night and were left deeply disappointed by a second defeat to the Toffees in just five days. The first half was a complete non-event with United looking and playing like an away team, barely getting out of their own half let alone troubling old nemesis Jordan Pickford. We were lucky to go into the half-time break goalless but the Blues broke the deadlock early on in the second period to leave the Toon desperate for a goal. As the Black and Whites finally woke up, it looked like an equaliser was secured when Elanga prodded the ball past Pickford at the back post. Unfortunately it rebounded off the upright, spun on the line and was hacked away to safety. Newcastle continued to push for a leveller but only really created a couple of decent chances, Wissa having a shot saved and Ramsey smashing an effort just wide. Unfortunately Ramsey also found the time to pick up two equally ludicrous yellow cards late on to ensure he received a red card and now has to serve a suspension to cap what was a miserable night for NUFC.

Fulham travelled to Aston Villa last weekend and were grateful for an absolute goalkeeping howler as they achieved a 1-1 draw. Behind at the break, Fulham were gifted an equaliser in the second half when the Villa ‘keeper dropped the ball over the line to ensure both sides would be able to enjoy a share of the points.

Newcastle have played three matches in London this season and won all of them without conceding a goal.

The Toon have lost their last two visits to Fulham.

NUFC have scored fourteen goals in their last seven games at Craven Cottage.

In 2003-04 Sir Bobby Robson was once again attempting to mastermind a return to the Champions League for his United side that had endured a difficult start to the season. An October trip to Fulham gave the Toon the opportunity to win their third match in a row but things got off to a disastrous opening when old boys Lee Clark and Louis Saha both found the net early on to give Fulham a two goal lead after just eight minutes. Thankfully this double setback spurred United into life and they gained a toe-hold in the match when Laurent Robert scored soon after with a half-volley. NUFC saved the real drama and excitement for the start of the second half when Alan Shearer twice found the net in front of incredulous away supporters. Our number nine kept his nerve to bury a spot-kick that brought the scores level after Ameobi was fouled in the area but even better to come. A few minutes after the equaliser, great link-up play with Jermain Jenas allowed Shearer the chance to put the Toon ahead and he made no mistake, rifling the ball into the roof of the net to send the travelling Toon Army delirious. Whilst this was undoubtedly one of the highlights of the season, it was also our last league victory away from home that campaign. Just two wins on our travels throughout the whole campaign meant that United would just miss out on a place in the Champions League. Fulham 2-3 Newcastle.

Philippe Albert is an absolute legend for those of us lucky enough to grow up in the mid-nineties. Signed by Kevin Keegan after a number of impressive performances at the 1994 World Cup, Albert soon proved that there was so much more than just defending to his game. Never afraid to bomb forward, he was often found at the other end of the pitch to good effect scoring a number of important goals. Although he’s best remembered for his sublime chip to end the scoring in a famous 5-0 victory over Man United, a personal favourite memory of mine is when he galloped forward to volley home an equally special effort in a 3-3 draw against Man City the previous season. Keegan was so impressed by Albert at Newcastle that he signed him again for Fulham in 1998 and was rewarded with two goals as the cottagers gained promotion from the second tier.

Louis Saha played on loan at Newcastle under Ruud Gullit in 1999 but managed only a handful of games. His only league strike came in a 4-1 home win against Coventry. He also netted a cracker away at Blackburn in the fifth round of the FA Cup. His winning goal set up a quarter-final tie with Everton as the Toon marched on to the Wembley final. He signed for Fulham in 2000 and scored over fifty league goals for the club, he was top scorer in the promotion campaign of 00/01 and was named in the PFA team of the year. He spent four years at Craven Cottage before moving on to Man United.

Danny Guthrie signed for the Toon in 2008 and spent four years on Tyneside, enduring the low of relegation in 2009 to the high of a top five Premier League finish in 2012. He was an integral part of our promotion in 2009-10, netting five goals and providing thirteen assists as we won the Championship. He played for Fulham on loan in 2015 but failed to find the net in six league appearances.

Matthias Jaissle after a 1-0 defeat at home to Everton: “They trained at a high level in the build-up, but when the ref started the game you couldn’t see that. It wasn’t the plan to shoot the long balls, it’s important to say that. It was not good enough and it was not brave enough to penetrate the last line. The goal came from an unforced error that led to a free-kick, but to be honest we were just sleeping. It’s so easy for them to take the quick free-kick and we were surprised. On a good day of course, Hornicek saves it. We have to stick together now, we have to show unity. It’s the only way. When the goals aren’t coming easily you lack confidence, it’s normal as a human being. We saw during the week that the quality is there but we need to take it to the pitch. It’s clear I have the responsibility to make it work as the manager of this club.”

Alvaro Arbeloa after a 1-1 draw away to Aston Villa: “I’m pleased with the team’s performance, especially in the second half. We were more aggressive, we controlled the tempo of the game, we had so many chances to score some goals, but in the end we couldn’t take the chances. I am happy because we knew before the match how difficult it would be to win here. Man City lost here one week ago and they are a Champions League team with a fantastic coach so, for me I’m really proud of my players because they showed ambition and character, and we played our way, which is the most important thing.”

As it is an away match, Newcastle United fans will not be collecting opposite the Gallowgate end, for the food bank. However, you can still help out and all online cash donations are very much appreciated. For further info and/or to donate to the food bank online.

This is a tough one to call. Newcastle have been desperately poor recently whilst Fulham have achieved some decent results after a poor start to their season. I’m old enough to remember the days when we couldn’t buy a win in London until a glorious night at Highbury in 2001 so have been delighted to see us achieve three wins in the capital already this season. Unfortunately, I don’t think this weekend will see a fourth. A poor game will see both teams having to be content with a point apiece. Fulham 0-0 Newcastle.

#2127. Midfielder’s surprising “Premier League team” claim ahead of Blackburn Rovers clash | West Ham News

Saturday’s Championship tie is the first league meeting of these two sides in fifteen years: The two sides have enjoyed very different histories since the 1 – 1 draw at Ewood Park in 2010. West Ham went on to European triumph in the interim, whilst for tomorrow’s hosts, their relegation from the Premier League in 2011/12 meant they went down as we went up, and the two sides haven’t met since apart from a 5 – 1 West Ham FA Cup victory in 2016.

Last time the two sides met one Mr Dmitri Payet was in full flow

Have no doubt that the hosts tomorrow are talking up their chances for the game, despite two big losses, as Blackburn see the visiting Hammers as the league’s glamour side, well beatable in their current reduced circumstances. No doubt hoping the early game vulnerabilities haven’t been fixed, the home side will do their best to come out all guns blazing and grab early goals.

Yahoo Sport feature comments from midfielder Kristi Montgomery, who is apparently ‘relishing’ the chance to test himself against a side he sees as being of Premier League quality:

“It’s the one that I’ve been looking forward to, to be honest with you,” Montgomery said.

“Just because my whole life, really, they’ve been a Premier League team, so that’s what I see them as, really. It’s a really good challenge and definitely a winnable game as well.

“It’s a massive test and a chance to show ourselves against one of the best teams in the league.

They’re in the Championship for a reason and there’s nothing to say that we can’t beat them.”

‘Fourteenth place for a reason’, Blackburn.

However upbeat Montgomery might sound, three losses in their last five outings means the form, as well as the ‘new manager bounce,‘ favours West Ham United who will be rocking up full of confidence after somehow snatching a point from Cardiff City on Wednesday night.

I’ll bet the last thing Blackburn manager Tony Mowbray wanted to hear in advance of this game was that the Irons had sacked Nuno and brought in ‘promotion specialist’ Scott Parker in his stead.

Certainly the new appointment has re-invigorated supporter engagement and I’ll bet there’s no more of that half time booing nonsense from the expected 7500 West Ham fans due for the game.

#2124. Liverpool transfer news: Reds in ‘advanced talks’ over new contract for player ‘trusted’ by Andoni Iraola

By Oliver Thomas | 05 Nov 2026 12:02

Liverpool have reportedly entered advanced negotiations with teenage starlet Trey Nyoni over a new contract.

The Reds suffered a disappointing 3-2 Champions League defeat away against Fenerbahce on Wednesday, but it was a memorable night for Nyoni who scored his first goal for the club.

At the age of 19 years and 127 days, Nyoni became the youngest player in the club's history to score his first goal for the team in a European Cup match, while he is Liverpool’s second youngest Champions League goalscorer after Trent Alexander-Arnold.

Nyoni has stepped up to Andoni Iraola’s first team this season after the Reds rejected a £30m offer from Nottingham Forest during the summer transfer window.

The academy graduate was handed his first Premier League start for Liverpool in their 1-0 defeat to champions Arsenal at Anfield last weekend and has played 12 times for the Reds across all competitions this term.

Nyoni has made a notable impression in Iraola’s midfield playing alongside either Alexis Mac Allister, Dominik Szoboszlai or Ryan Gravenberch, and the youngster could soon be rewarded with an improved deal.

According to The Athletic, Nyoni is in advanced talks with Liverpool over extending his contract, even though his current deal runs until June 2030.

The report adds that Nyoni has been discussing his future with Liverpool for 'months', with the club keen to reward him with fresh terms to reflect his first-team emergence under Iraola.

While a contract extension has yet to be finalised, it is understood that there is optimism that an agreement will be reached, with a breakthrough in negotiations expected soon.

Speaking to reporters before Liverpool’s loss to Fenerbahce, Iraola made it clear that he believes Nyoni is now “in a very good place” to enhance his development.

“Trey just has to continue in the same way as since the beginning of pre-season, be ready for all of the games,” said the Spaniard.

“We trust him, he’s doing very well. We have to encourage him to continue learning, improving and getting experience. But he’s in a very good place.”

With Gravenberch facing a spell on the sidelines through injury and Szoboszlai having only just recovered from an injury of his own, Nyoni is a strong contender to start again for Liverpool in Sunday’s Premier League clash against Crystal Palace.

#2123. Arsenal maintain perfect start but lack firepower of rivals

Bukayo Saka maintained Arsenal’s perfect start to the season, but Mikel Arteta appeared to acknowledge that the Premier League champions are in danger of leaving themselves short in attack.

There is still time for Arteta to add another forward to his squad and whether he does so or not could be important, with the transfer window closing on Tuesday night.

Having sold Leandro Trossard and with Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus on the verge of moves away, Arsenal appear light of forward options.

Lyon winger Malick Fofana has been offered to the club, but he is an underwhelming target given Morgan Rogers and Vinícius Júnior were pursued earlier in the summer.

“We are trying to improve the squad,” Arteta, the Arsenal head coach, said. “Until Tuesday night, we’re going to try to do that. I’ve been disconnected from the world for 24 hours because I think my energy and focus has to be on the match. I will give it [my energy] now.”

Asked if he currently has enough depth in forward positions, Arteta added: “It depends if everybody is fit or not. We know that the depth has to be really big when you are fighting for four competitions. So we’re going to try to do that.”

This was an Aston Villa team there for the taking after being gutted by their Premier League rivals and still waiting for new signings to be ready to play and gel.

But Arsenal made hard work of their victory and one senses there will be more games like this if Arteta has to rely on what he has already got until at least January.

Chelsea are showing they can score goals for fun having spent £117m on Rogers. Manchester City are strengthening their firepower with the signing of Iliman Ndiaye and Bradley Barcola has joined Liverpool. Arsenal have the defence and the midfield, but not necessarily the depth of quality in forward positions of their rivals.

0.52 - Arsenal faced the fewest shots (11), the fewest shots on target (1) and allowed their opponents the lowest xG (0.52) across the first two matchdays of the Premier League season.🔒 Locked. pic.twitter.com/blSUAeqoLb

Christos Tzolis is the lone attacking signing to date and there was evidence at Villa Park that it will be a risk to rely too heavily on the Greek winger.

Tzolis had made an exciting start to his Arsenal career in the Community Shield and the first Premier League victory over Coventry City, but he had to be taken off at half-time on Monday night.

The former Club Brugge winger not only lost out to Matty Cash, but was also at the centre of Villa appeals for him to be sent off.

Tzolis had already been booked for a foul on Cash, when, in the 36th minute, he appeared to foul John McGinn as Villa broke from the edge of their own penalty area.

McGinn appealed that Tzolis should have been shown a second yellow card, but referee Jarred Gillett let the Arsenal man off the hook.

Arteta was wise to take Tzolis off at the break and his replacement, Eberechi Eze, had a hand in what proved to be Arsenal’s 59th-minute winner.

Eze slipped in Riccardo Calafiori and Saka got in front of Ian Maatsen to poke the Arsenal full-back’s low cross into the net. Saka’s goal had been the first shot on target in the game.

"It's a brilliant goal, it really is" 👏 Bukayo Saka gives Arsenal the lead at Villa Park! pic.twitter.com/aV7DA8cARL

Just before the goal, Arsenal thought they had been awarded a penalty. Ross Barkley lost possession with a sloppy pass, allowing Declan Rice to advance towards the Villa penalty area. He played the ball through for Saka and Maatsen barged into the back of the winger.

Gillett paused before pointing to the spot, but a VAR check showed that Maatsen’s foul had taken place outside the penalty area and Martin Odegaard fired the resulting free-kick wide.

The goal and the overturned penalty were pretty much it for Arsenal in terms of threatening the hosts, for whom goalkeeper Zion Suzuki made his debut. Suzuki did not have much to do with his hands, but impressed with his distribution.

It was Villa who went closest to scoring in the first half, through one of the club’s five surviving members of last season’s Europa League-winning team.

Emiliano Buendia scored Villa’s second goal in the final against Freiburg and the Argentine rattled the Arsenal crossbar with a 20-yard shot that had beaten visiting goalkeeper David Raya.

Before then, McGinn had sent a shot over Raya’s bar and into the building site where Villa are redeveloping the club’s old North Stand.

Buendia, McGinn, Cash, Pau Torres and Victor Lindelof are the only Villa players to have started the Europa League final who have not left this summer.

Defender Ezri Konsa is one of Villa’s Europa League winners to have departed and he made his Arsenal debut as a late substitute. The defender received a mixed reception, as he was first booed by some home fans but was then applauded.

Other than hitting the bar in the opening 45 minutes, Villa squandered a chance for a quick reply to Arsenal’s opener when McGinn hesitated instead of shooting after being played in by Nicolas Jackson.

Jackson lasted 71 minutes for Villa in what proved to be a promising debut. In the first half, he raced away down the right before sending the ball across the six-yard box. But there was no team-mate on hand to convert.

One of Villa’s other summer signings, Alejandro Garnacho, is yet to make an impact for his new club. The Argentine got an earful from manager Unai Emery for not being ready to go on. He eventually replaced Ross Barkley, but could not help conjure an equaliser.

This is the start Arteta wanted. But, in attacking positions, Arsenal will finish the transfer window weaker than they started it if the club are not active in the final hours of the transfer window. And that could prove costly.

We lost. We competed well. They won the league last year. We are trying to build a team but a lot of positive things [beyond] the result. How we competed. How it was progressively better. We didn’t create clear chances. Some players made fantastic debuts. Suzuki and Jackson did very good work. I think it’s the first step forward and positive for the next matches.

Accepting this result, I think we had chances to draw the match but we are in our rebuild. It is the way [ahead for us] making these changes and I say to the supporters and players that the message is there in the way we played.

To lose one match is painful but after the pain we must try to get positive things, This is the reason I am optimistic. There are 38 matches we played two. We haven’t one point but we can get better hopefully. And we will get players [Mbaye and Harwood-Bellis].

We can feel confidence because how we want to build the team again is true, to compete like today.

I think the squad we have now is how we planned with the  players we wanted.

[Are you confident you have replaced the quality that has gone?] Yes.

I’m really happy. It’s a big win. It’s a tough place to come and earn the three points but I think we deserved it.

It was a game where 11 was not enough and the finishers came in and did a magnificent job to win it. I know how tough it is to win here.

Every big team struggles against them for the past four years because they are so good. They are well coached, have great players. Great in transition. The moment you lose the ball and let them run inside they are really dangerous but I love a lot of the things I saw from my team.

Ebs [Eze] creates the action that sees us win the game, Bruno with Mikel [Merino] in midfield changed the dynamic of it, Ezri [Konsa] really composed and calm with every decision he made and then Zubi… I’m really happy with all of them.

Every game in the Premier League it’s like [you’re saying] we have to win this game. We know the level. We know how difficult it is in this league.

[Can you sign Julian Alvarez tomorrow?] I don’t know. That’s for the people upstairs.

It was a very tough match. Aston Villa’s defensive setup made things difficult for us, constantly catching us offside. We couldn’t attack as comfortably as we did last week. But as you know, sometimes one goal is enough for us. We have a very strong defence.

Today, we were great out of possession too and didn’t allow transition attacks.

I keep my targets for myself. Every week I want to be there and try decide the game as that’s what I’m in the team to do. That’s my mentality.

[Have you seen Chelsea?] I’ve seen them. [What do you think?] We’ll see on Sunday.

Jamie Carragher explains how Arsenal broke Aston Villa down for their winning goal 🔎 pic.twitter.com/CAI8zhznrJ

Arsenal host Chelsea on Sunday at 4.30pm while Villa go to Hull City at 5.30pm on Saturday. It’s too early for a must-win game for Villa who showed some positive signs tonight but they could certainly do with one.

Arsenal win with a performance of efficiency and patience that emphasises their superiority when asked to grind out a result.

John McGinnis arguing the toss with the referee about his belief that he was fouled in the box in the dying seconds. It was outside the box and if Maatsen’s ‘tackle’ wasn’t a foul, neither was Gabriel’s.

Not sure the way of refereeing that lets a lot of calls go and waits for VAR is going to enhance the game.

Maatsen tackles Bruno Guimaraes in the Villa box with an ugly lunge in which he appears to scissor him, kicking his heel with one leg before knocking the ball away with the other but the referee deems it fair and VAR lets it pass, too.

Arsenal’s game management is working well as usual until Raya goes too long and the ball bounces through to Suzuki. But when he starts a counter-attack Alysson ends it with a dive and back come Arsenal.

Maatsen slides in late on Saka down the right, bypasses the ball and crashes into his shin. Yellow card.

Aston Villa probe but Arsenal hold them 30 yards from goal and when they do slide pass down the side of a defender for Buendia to chase, Bruno is ideally positioned to cover and make the block which he celebrates as if he were Leonardo Bonucci.

Eight minutes of stoppage time are signalled by the fourth official.

Suzuki races 15 yards outside his box to head a long pass away from Havertz to McGinn. Back come Arsenal after McGinn is squeezed off the ball but Wan-Bisska wins it back with a fine tackle. He is among the best one-on-one pure defenders in the league.

Zubimendi rattles Buendia’s bones in a crunching but legal tackle.

That was Rice’s last contribution as he limps off. He is probably OK but wise to withdraw him if he has had a twinge.

Maatsen drives down the left and cuts into the box. White leans into him, Rice guides him with a rigid left arm and the rampaging left-back loses his feet. Maatsen acknowledges Rice’s fine defending when he gets back up.

Quite a few outside observers questioned why Arsenal signed Konsa. This apparent injury to Mosquera is the reason. With Saliba out for months and Timber still struggling to regain his fitness, Mosquera was the only right-sided centre-back in the squad (unless they repurposed White, who is needed at right back).

Garnacho faces up Saka after being played down the left by Buendia but his cross is blocked by the goalscorer. Raya catches the resulting corner.

McGinn wipes out Merino from behind and is deservedly booked. Moments earlier Alysson was also booked for leaving one on Gabriel after the centre-half had cleared the ball, choosing not to put on the brakes and bodychecking him instead.

Unai Emery has just gone ballistic at substitute Alejandro Garnacho.

Emery clearly wasn’t happy with Garnacho not being ready to come on and let the Chelsea loanee know about it.

And Mosquera cannot continue having overstretched so it’s a debut for the former Villa stalwart who is greeted warmly.

Suzuki saves in a one-on-one with Havertz running through from 40 yards, waiting and refusing to go down and make things easy for Havertz, sticking up a right arm to block the shot. But he may have been offside which may mitiagte it in terms of not costing Arsenal anything but he really should have beaten the keeper.

Nice pass from Merino to set the hare running.

Barkley plays a diagonal pass across the turf out to Alysson on the right and he hares round Calafiori to cross from the byline but could not get the ball past Gabriel at the near post.

Now Maatsen goes flying but this time in the Arsenal box under a challenge from White that was a duplicate of the one 30 seconds before. ‘Premier League corrupt as f---,’ sing the Villa fans, ignoring the similarities between the two incidents. The defenders’ arms made contact with the attacking players but without the force to send them sprawling.

Havertz hits the deck in the Villa penalty area when challenged by Kamara as they fought for Odegaard’s scooped dink from the right.

Bruno Guimaraes and Mikel Merino are stripped and ready to come on.

Once again, it’s Riccardo Calafiori who opens up the opposition’s defence with his off-the-ball running. He is the one player in this Arsenal team who makes genuinely unpredictable and unexpected movements.

McGinn’s combination with Jackson looks promising and the centre-forward invites him to bullock forward down the inside-right channel with a clever pass but the Villa captain is soon swamped by yellow shirts and the ball gets stuck beneath his feet.

Gary Neville makes the fair point that one of Arsenal’s most unheralded qualities is their patience. Their confidence in their rock-solid defence does not make them reckless but they are always confident of finding a way. They trust the method implicitly.

Aston Villa 0 Arsenal 1 (Saka) Mosquera has the ball 25 yards out, left of centre, he strokes it to Eze who angles a pass to Calafiori running between Cash and Lindelof. He makes it to the byline and cuts back a low cross that Saka and Maatsen both lunge at and the Arsenal winger gets there first to turn it in.

"It's a brilliant goal, it really is" 👏 Bukayo Saka gives Arsenal the lead at Villa Park! pic.twitter.com/aV7DA8cARL

Rice, Eze and Odegaard stand over it. Rive walks away and Odegaard approaches the ball with a semi-circular run-up. He whips it over the wall and about a foot wide of the left post. Suzuki was stranded but no matter.

It was outside the box. Not all that sure it was a foul either. But Arsenal will have a free-kick.

Maatsen and Saka collide as they chase a Rice pass that Saka would never reach. Seemed to be outside the box.

It has been fairly dull fare so far as two systems and structures that cede little space clash.

Lindelof rises high to meet Rice;s dipping cross from the right as Havertz, on his shoulder, was poised to pounce. He heads it straight up and Suzuki leaps to catch it.

Now Barkley picks out a diagonal to send Jackson down the left. The centre-forward reaches the 18-yard line, cuts inside and works it over to McGinn who lofts a cross over Villa’s back-post runners and out of play.

Eze did his best work from the left last season. Villa start with Barkley scoop-chipping a pass from the middle out to the left, 40 yards upfield. Maatsen runs on to it and drives past White to ram a shot into the side-netting.

Arsenal were too slow to move the ball forward in that first half, and too loose with it when they did get into promising positions. There’s a lack of urgency in their passing. I wonder if we’ll see Bruno Guimarães soon… one of the reasons they signed him was to add more quick forward passing to their play.

Signs of encouragement for Villa without creating much while Arsenal have been stymied so far by Villa’s neutering of Tzolis and the left wing. Arsenal’s right-sided trio – White, Odegaard and Saka – look the most likely to create something.

Only a minute of added time to be played. Arsenal still lacking a spark, largely because there’s a lack of precision in their forward, line-breaking passing.

Villa will be very happy with this half. Much more like their old selves in terms of structure and organisation.

Calafiori’s throw to Gabriel is picked off by Jackson down the right and he dribbles down the right. He is forced to slow down to wait for a midfield runner. When Hemmings catches up, so have three Arsenal defenders and though Jackson bends in a low, cross to the edge of the six-yard box it is about 18 inches away from Hemmings’ reach.

Calafiori goes down in the Villa box when Pau Torres uses his arm to lever him away as they tracked the flight of a cross. The referee sees nothing wring in it and neither does VAR.

Gillett takes an age to stop the play when Cash uses his body to shove Tzolis over after the winger had played a pass. Cash obviously thinks he has rattled the new signing and is keen to rough him up some more. The ref does award a free-kick but only after that daft delay.

Tzolis loses the ball on the edge of the Villa penalty area, tackled by McGinn. The captain slots a straight pass up to Buendia who tries to bend a pass into Jackson’s stride as he sprinted down the inside right channel but Gabriel read the trajectory and got there first.

Suzuki picks out McGinn with a long pass. He feeds it to Buendia who gives Hemmings a chance to chase it down the left. Arsenal shuffle over in defence so he doubles back and returns the ball to Buendia. The No 10 whips over a dipping cross looking for Barkley and Jackson but Calafiori and Raya make sure the goalkeeper wins it.

We’ve not seen much from Christos Tzolis on Arsenal’s left wing so far. He’s been excellent since joining the club this summer but he’s hardly seen the ball in this opening half an hour and he’s just been booked after losing a battle with Matty Cash.

Arsenal free-kick 30 yards out, left of centre, for a foul on Lewis-Skelly who was artfully shielding the ball. Odegaard chips to the right post but Havertz heads it back across the box rather than going for goal and Villa clear.

Cash gets the better of Tzolis again in the tackle and then Suzuki sprays a perfect 60-yard pass out to Hemmings that Gary Neville, likening it to something Ederson was capable of delivering for Man City, one of the best goalkeeper passes he has ever seen. Tzolis was booked for stopping Cash running off with the ball.

Maatsen, who could never dislodge Digne for long, has a chance now to make the position his won. He strides down the left, exploiting Rice’s positioning error but his right-foot isn’t half as good as his left and his bending effort is scuffed far too straight and easily cleared.

Saka drives down the right after a neat Odegaard, Saka, White triangle. Pau Torres races over to toe the ball behind for a corner. Saka takes and Rice flicks it on at the near post and Suzuki tips it over. No corner, though, as Gabriel had rag-dolled McGinn at the back post after the Villa captain had backed in to him and tried to stop him making a run into the middle.

“Champions of Europe, you’ll never sing that.” Villa fans poke the wound.

Arsenal are finding it difficult to play through the middle of the pitch but have found Saka in space on the right wing on a few occasions already. Villa are congesting the central areas, where Odegaard does his best work.

Calafiori picks off Kamara’s pass looking, for the third or fourth time, to play someone, usually Jackson, in behind the left-back. A minute later Calafiori challenges McGinn for a bouncing, loose ball and stoops to use his head. colliding with McGinn’s boot. Was the head low or the boot high? Arsenal think the latter but the ref sides, rightly, with McGinn.

Arsenal corner on the left. The threat inherent every time Rice is in a quadrant diminished on this occasion because Mosquera barged Cash just after Rice struck the ball. Free-kick to Villa.

Timber may be preferred by Arteta at right-back but Saka prefers White. The two have a well-grooved partnership in tersm of who underlaps and who overlaps. They never seem to get in each other’s way.

Bukayo Saka does seem to be getting a lot of time and space on the right flank.

It’s looking a risky tactic by Villa at the moment as the England international is being invited to cut in towards the penalty area.

Havertz is played down the inside-right channel in the penalty area by a cute Odegaard pass bur he blazes his shot across goal and wide of the left post. A replay shows he was offside but even so it was a lazy finish.

Kamara grabs Tzolis round the waist from behind and when the winger hits the deck, rounds him and passus to Buendia who crashes a right-foot diagonal shot on to the bar from 20 yards. The ref did not see it as a foul despite Arsenal’s protestations but had it gone in it would have given VAR a dilemma.

Worth keeping an eye on Aston Villa midfielder George Hemmings tonight.

He is only a teenager and has emerged from Villa’s academy, but Unai Emery is already a huge fan.

Hemmings produced a highly promising performance in the Super Cup against Paris Saint-Germain earlier this month.

Suzuki misjudges the flight of Rice’s typically menacing corner and flaps at it but his defenders and an offside flag leave him without egg on his face.

McGinn stops Calafiori down the left then gives the ball straight to Tzolis. The Greece winger opens his body and passes to Lewis-Skelly who shoots with his right foot from the left of the 18-yard line. Cash slides in to block the shot and it loops over the bar for a corner.

Hemmings uses his strength to hold off Ben White and shift the ball inside to McGinn who wraps his left instep around a shot and wafts it into building site behind Raya’s goal.

Ibrahim Mbaye and Taylor Harwood-Bellis are in the directors’ box watching the game. Villa don’t look like a hastily assembled team.

Suzuki knocks the ball long with his left foot, looking for Jackson but the ball spins away from him to Raya who boots it back upfield. McGinn pounces on it, turns past Rice and plays Cash in down the right. He crosses towards the near post and Mosquera hooks it clear.

Arsenal kick off with Odegaard spinning and trying to play Saka in down the right as they defend the empty North Stand end. The ball skids off the turf and Saka can’t trap it. The ball goes out for a Villa throw-in.

Who dies in the summer and played for both clubs.

Arsenal are in fact in yellow and navy. My mistake.

Villa in claret and blue with a twist, the shorts are blue for the first time since, I think 2001. Arsenal are in yellow and black. Leeds, like Arsenal, have traditionally worn yellow and blue as their away strip but have been shunted into yellow and black as well by Adidas this season.

There are a few guys standing in the North Stand with hard hats on, and it appears they are on ball retrieval duty.

They will be on red alert for any wayward shots that land in the empty stand.

Warm reception for Ezri Konsa from Villa’s fans as he walked back to the tunnel with Arsenal’s substitutes.

Konsa joined Arsenal last week for £51m, ending a spell of seven years at Villa Park.

Wonder if the likes of Morgan Rogers and Emiliano Martinez will get a similar reception when they return here with Chelsea.

Aston Villa  Suzuki; Cash, Lindelof, Torres, Maatsen; Kamara, Barkley; McGinn, Buendía, Hemmings; Jackson. Substitutes  Bizot, Mings, Ruggeri, Garnacho, Abraham, Bogarde, Wan-Bissaka, Edward, Lynch.

Arsenal  Raya; White, Mosquera, Gabriel, Calafiori; Lewis-Skelly, Rice; Saka, Odegaard, Tzolis; Havertz. Substitutes  Arrizabalaga, Hincapié, Eze, Gyokeres, Konsa, Madueke, Merino, Zubimendi, Guimaraes.

Zion Suzuki is one of two debuts for Aston Villa tonight and there is a genuine buzz of excitement around the Japan international.

Suzuki was signed from Parma for £30m as the replacement for Emiliano Martinez and arrives with a stellar reputation.

He’s got big boots – and gloves – to fill, but Unai Emery is convinced he will become a future star at Villa Park.

The other debutant is record £65m signing Nicolas Jackson, who joined last week from Chelsea.

Good evening. Yes, the first match was not as planned but we must keep going forward. Today we are playing our first home match and I am looking forward. We need to try as soon as possible to get our best individuals fit for a good performance. And today is a good match for us. Ir is difficult but always with our supporters here we feel comfortable and confident. Hopefully we can transmit our positive energy to our supporters.

We lost the first game but it is not a [team full of rookies]. We have experienced players. They play with energy and know how we want to play. We have to adapt with Suzuki but we have confidence [in him]. Jackson, the striker, and other players, George Hemmings, he is young but played fantastically in pre-season. He knows how we want to play.

Today is a challenge but I’m really looking forward to how the players will respond collectively, individually. We know we are changing things but no excuses. We have to perform today, we have to try to adapt the new players, to build our team to get their best today.

I am positive and I am optimistic. The players are ready.

Aston Villa are in a transition period and rebuilding on and off the field.

Unai Emery’s 2.0 have been under construction all summer and there could be 10 new signings in by tomorrow morning.

Villa have of course lost six of the starting XI from last season’s Europa League final, with Morgan Rogers, Ollie Watkins, Ezri Konsa, Youri Tielemans, Emiliano Martinez and Lucas Digne all departing this summer.

The North Stand at Villa Park, which faces the iconic Holte End, is also under renovation and closed down for tonight’s game.

It could be a bit quieter tonight but there is still a mood of optimism among Villa fans, despite such a summer of change.

We have had a real block of training sessions to work on things and prepare for this game in the right way.

We will have time to make changes throughout the game [on why he has picked an unchanged team]. They did really well [against Coventry] and for the game we expect [tonight] they have the right qualities to hurt them and that’s how we start.

They have that [upheaval in personnel] but they have been with Unai for a long time, they are a super well-coached team and we know how tough it is always to come here. We are very conscious of that but also very ambitious.

That’s the way we want to play [with aggression] constantly from the first minute, to suffocate the opponent and be better than them.

[Does it being your 250th Arsenal Premier League game add something special to it?] Just to win [makes it special].

She wore… she wore… she wore a yellow ribbon …

Two changes – Zion Suzuki and Nicolas Jackson make debuts. Joao Gomes misses the match as the first of his three-game suspension and Marco Bizot drops to the bench.

Double debuts 🤩Your Villa XI to face Arsenal this evening 👋 pic.twitter.com/Zue0ZTSJt9

Arteta names unchanged starting XI but Bruno Guimaraes is fit for the bench. Ezri Konsa joins him there.

🟡 𝗧𝗘𝗔𝗠𝙉𝙀𝙒𝙎 🔵Unchanged for Monday night football 🔐🤝 Presented by @deel pic.twitter.com/ptvpKHDahn

In its rightful place 🏠🏆 pic.twitter.com/FMH4zve1aD

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League match between Aston Villa and Arsenal from Villa Park. The champions travel to the team that finished fourth last season in buoyant mood and form despite some misgivings within their fanbase about their recruitment this summer.

It amounts so far to making Pier Hincapié‘s loan into a proper transfer, revamping the left wing with Christos Tzolis replacing Leandro Trossard and Gabriel Martinelli, upgrading options in central midfield by buying Bruno Guimarães and selling Cristian Norgaard – and signing Ezri Konsa from today’s opponents to give them the greatest elite defensive depth that I can recall at club since Manchester City’s Treble winners had Kyle Walker, Ruben Dias, John Stones, Nathan Aké, João Cancelo, Aymeric Laporte, Manuel Akanji, Rico Lewis and Sergio Gómez on the books at the same time.

Villa, by contrast, have endured a turbulent summer of trading with the departures of Europa League winners Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans, Lucas Digne, the aforementioned Konsa, Ollie Watkins and Emi Martínez, raising, along with other departures, more than £315m. They have spent about £180m to remodel the team though Johan Manzambi, who is injured, and João Gomes, who is suspended after his red card in the 4-0 defeat by Brighton, are absent tonight.

We can expect to see Zion Suzuki, Matteo Ruggeri and hopefully Nicolas Jackson and Leon Goretzka who have been registered in time to play, plus the loan signings Aaron Wan-Bissaka and Alejandro Garnacho. Still to come are the pending purchases of Taylor Harwood-Bellis and Ibrahim Mbaye in a process that emphasises how profoundly Villa are invested in and dependent upon their manager, Unai Emery.

After so much upheaval, it would be foolish to set much store on Villa’s 2-1 victory last season, sealed by Emi Buendía’s winner in the fifth minute of stoppage time. Arsenal barely broke sweat in blowing Man City away in the Community Shield and cakewalked to victory over Coventry in the league’s opening fixture. His past work suggests Emery will be able to forge another formidable side from his talented new squad but this match feels two months too soon for him against his old club.

#2122. Blackburn v West Ham | Familiar tactics planned to bring Parker’s brave new world back down to earth

Another Saturday afternoon kick-off beckons in this crazy Championship season which offers ‘feast or famine’ football. The second international break kicks in after todays game, with a further maddening two week hiatus after the Hammers’ latest three games in eight days physical assault course.

Surprisingly, only Kyle Walker Peters appears on the ‘injury list’ for West Ham, despite 14 league and 3 cup games already undertaken. Compared with our opponents today who have several players likely out injured, West Ham’s mixture of good luck and good player management seems to be doing the trick again this season, as it did last.

Walker Peters is likely to be the sole enforced absentee in Scott Parker’s match day squad

Speaking ahead of the game, Blackburn Rovers’ veteran coach Tony Mowbray evidently plans to reprise the tactics deployed by Millwall, Southampton, Cardiff and others -and expose West Ham’s well known early defensive frailties:

“”They’re beatable. They’ve lost their manager because they’ve lost too many games this year already and I haven’t seen a team that I think, ‘wow, they’re miles too good for us’.

“Swansea might give that impression, but I think we should be positive, aggressive, play on the front foot and try our hand and see how we get on against West Ham United.” (lancashiretelegraph.co.uk)

West Ham fans will hope to see a more confident, solid foundation created in just a few days – more than Nuno managed to instil in over a year: A tough ask, which is why it may still be far too soon to expect wholesale change.

Scoring the first goal – or two – would prove something of a welcome relief to the 7000 expected Irons fans travelling to the game today, who will all be aware of the Hammers’ terrible propensity to concede first.

As will Parker. Let’s see if he’s managed to instil, at the very least a new combative spirit in his players, and continue on with Wednesday’s second half mentality. Because the Hammers cannot rely on coming back from the dead every week.

From the old Bobby Moore Upper to the Billy Bonds' stand these days - I've been watching since '03 and a supporter since about 1970.. Favourite player - Dean Ashton: Curse you Shaun Wright-Phillips. I still watch YouTube repeats of the Cup Final of 2006 hoping in vain that Shaka Hislop grows another six inches and stops Steven Gerrard's injury time equaliser. Can tell I'm getting old knowing I watched both Mark Noble's debut and his last game at West Ham. “Good player management seems to be doing the trick again this season, as it did the last” ? What ?, getting us relegated, again !

After ex Hammer Nathan Trott played a blinder against us on Wednesday, there are two more ex youth team players that have been playing on the wings for Blackburn, Fevrier and Afolayan. Blackburn played on Tuesday and so had an extra day to recover, let’s hope these ex Irons aren’t as inspired as Nathan was.

Should be a contrast of styles between the two managers, both on and off the pitch. Should be a very interesting game re. starting XI, new faces making an appearance. Magassa, Orford, Soucek or Alvarez? Although I wonder if Orford is built to be a no 10 like Mukasa, once he has time enough to settle into the role as Mukasa has – see so little of him so don’t really know.

There is a disadvantage to that in that if they don’t go ahead then they’ve expended a lot of energy and championship benches do not contain a lot of quality.

It’s also been seen how we overwhelm in the second half once they do run out of puff and quality.

My tactic would be to soak it up first half, not go behind, then nick it second half once they’ve blown themselves out. Should work but only for as long as it’s seen to be working and teams change their tactics again.

We’ve been seen to have a weakness and teams will try to exploit it until we stop them.

As a Newcastle United fan, have a look at these Premier League fixtures on Saturday and have a think about what you’d like to happen and what is most likely in terms of results.

My conclusions and predictions on these Saturday matches now coming up:

The five draws have been three 1-1s and two goalless draws. I fancy 0-0 or 1-1 today.

Arsenal are grinding the results out without looking particularly good. They won 1-0 at Liverpool with pretty much their only big clear chance of the game and at Forest they scored with their only shot on target. In between they won 2-0 against Everton but were fortunate to do so.

#2120. SPFL star targets goal rush after finally breaking his Premiership duck

Joel Cotterill is determined to add to his goal tally at St Johnstone after breaking his scoring duck for the Perth side last weekend.

The 22-year-old attacking midfielder, who signed for Simo Valakari’s side from Swansea City in September, notched a dramatic leveller on his eighth appearance as the 10-men Perth side fought out a 2-2 William Hill Premiership draw with Kilmarnock at Rugby Park.

Ahead of Saturday’s visit from Dundee, for whom Cotterill played on loan last season, the former Wales Under-21 player said: “It’s something that I want to build on massively. There’s no better feeling than getting it in that kind of game as well.

“I just need to build on that now and try to get more as the season progresses. I think that’s a big part of my game that I’m missing at the moment: goals. I think I get into the right area sometimes, but it’s just something that I need to get better at in my game.

“That weekend is a good stepping stone for me now to just carry on and get as many as I can.”

St Johnstone have had four draws in the last six games to sit in seventh place, and Cotterill knows the next step is obvious and important. He said: “If you look at the games where we’ve had draws, we’ve been very unlucky. We had a sending off last weekend.

“But the togetherness we have and that spirit we have as a group, I think if we have 11 players on the pitch, we could give anyone a good game in this league, and we’ve shown that already.

“So I think we need to turn these draws that we’re having into getting the three points and coming away with a win. Dundee are very aggressive. Really good on the ball when the ball’s on the floor in play.

“I think they’ve got very, very good outlets and wingers, very quick, very direct. But I’m excited, I’m really excited for the game.

"I think it’s going to be a really good test for both teams.”

#2119. West Ham winger has to prove the Tottenham doubters wrong – here’s how

West Ham United and Tottenham Hotspur seem to be holding their noses and doing transfer business with each other after a feud between the two club chairmen prohibited any sort of contact in well over a decade. Now that both Levy and Sullivan have departed, the two seem prepared to trade players once again.

The two sets of fans, of course, revel in player misfortune once transfers have taken place – how West Ham supporters enjoyed Mohammed Kudus’ first season travails and then merely taking £85 million from the Spuds for the signature of Mateus Fernandes and doubling our money seemed sufficient cause for satisfaction.

Quietly banking about £20 million more than the young Portuguese would generate from any other club and heading off financial armageddon with north London money seemed a deal well done.

Spurs fans now have their moment, with the gloating evident over Manor Solomon‘s failure to launch in east London. The winger has struggled despite frequent starting slots under Nuno and must now be facing competition from young Edvin Austbø who has impressed each time he’s stepped onto the turf.

As Tottenham fan site Hotspurhq.com puts it:

“West Ham are saddled with Manor Solomon, who has scored just 2 goals with 2 assists in 14 appearances. The big problem with Solomon that Tottenham have been well aware of is that he is not a team player.

Spurs had to listen to a lot of complaining from him about his minutes or about mistreatment from the club, but the real reason why he didn’t play was because he never showed he was good enough.”

Solomon – there’s a man of the match in there lurking – but many doubt he can he return to that form once again

Identifying the problem as being specifically to do with his mindset rather than his ability, the criticism goes on:

“A big part of that is Solomon does not help his teams win. He holds the ball too much and plays like someone more focused on scoring or piling up his own stats than playing with the team.”

Early on this season, after his man of the match award, there was a feeling that we’d stolen Solomon for a very modest £4 million up – front: Depending on what a decent coaching regime can coax out of the Israeli, there may still be room for quiet satisfaction.

He has the record and the ability, but needs to find a way to return to his best form. When in a Leeds eleven, he looked a top quality prospect indeed and along with Joel Piroe scored 29 times, playing no small part in taking the club back to the Premier League.

Much like his new manager, he’s done it before and knows what is needed. The jury is out as to whether he’s still got it.

#2118. Fortuna Sittard vs Telstar - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adepoju Marvellous | 05 Nov 2026 12:26

High-flying Fortuna Sittard return to Eredivisie action this weekend, hosting Telstar at the Fortuna Sittard Stadion on Saturday.

The home side begin this weekend’s round of fixtures in sixth place with 19 points - 10 places and 10 points clear of the visitors.

A trip to Feyenoord, who had won three straight meetings between the teams, threatened to end Fortuna’s six-game unbeaten run, especially after Luciano Valente opened the scoring just before the hour mark. However, Shiloh ‘t Zand equalised with four minutes remaining to force a share of the spoils.

While some may argue the point flattered Danny Buijs’s men given their performance, it was a reward for their resilience, a quality they have displayed in abundance since a 5-1 drubbing at the hands of Ajax in mid-September.

Having collected just seven points from a possible 15 in Sittard-Geleen, Fortuna’s return to form still has room for improvement via consistent results at home. A 1-0 win over Excelsior in their last home outing suggests they are moving in the right direction.

Bottom of the league in average ball possession this term (35.7%), Fortuna remain a side best known for their off-the-ball work. They finished second-bottom in this metric last season, only ahead of relegated Heracles.

With each of their next six matches coming against teams currently below them in the table, Fortuna have an opportunity to build a sustained run of positive results and enter the second half of the season well positioned for a European push.

After almost three months, Telstar finally ended their wait for a first victory since beating NEC Nijmegen on the opening weekend, running out emphatic 4-2 winners over FC Utrecht in Sunday’s clash at BUKO Stadion.

The victory came at a crucial time for manager Henk Brugge, who was under increased scrutiny after his side were knocked out of the KNVB Beker first round by lower-league opposition Almere City just four days earlier.

Two points adrift of safety, another Telstar defeat this weekend could pile the pressure back on Brugge and their away record this season has been dismal, with just one win, four points, and four goals scored from five matches on the road.

However, De Witte Leeuwen are unbeaten in their last five trips to the Fortuna Sittard Stadion dating back to August 2014, and will draw confidence from their most recent trip in March, when they cruised to a 4-1 victory.

Facing a side with the best big-chance conversion rate in the division (76.9%), Saturday’s visitors will be wary of conceding too many opportunities, despite boasting a significant advantage in clear-cut chances created (23-10).

Rodrigo Guth and Lequincio Zeefuik both limped off with injuries in Fortuna’s last outing and are doubtful for Saturday’s clash.

This could open the door for Ivan Marquez and Kristoffer Peterson - both substitutes last time out - to come into the hosts’ starting lineup.

Twenty-one-year-old Gerald Alders has missed Telstar’s last three outings and remains a doubt for this weekend.

Patrick Brouwer and Rui Mendes were also absent against Utrecht, although the former is likely to return to action in Sittard.

Tyrone Owusu has scored five goals and provided one assist in his last five matches for the visitors, making the midfielder one to watch.

Fortuna Sittard possible starting lineup:

Branderhorst; Pinto, Van Ottele, Marquez, Hubner, Dahlhaus; Ihattaren, Descotte, Brittijn, ‘t Zand; Zeefuik

Koeman Jr; Peersman, Soualhia, Valk, Caschili; Rossen, Ahmed; Demircan, Owusu, Martha; Thorisson

Fortuna are playing their best football in some time, and that momentum makes them strong favourites to edge an out-of-sorts Telstar side.

We expect the home side to make light work of their visitors and head into the international break on a high.
