🇮🇹 Sentendo il calore dell'Italia! 🥰🇬🇧 Feeling the warmth of Italy! 🥰 pic.twitter.com/ze6Ww1Z0zx

The session starts in around 40 minutes, so drivers are on their Gameboys and Instagram, and reading the weekend edition of The Telegraph.

Words we live by, this weekend and always ❤️ pic.twitter.com/0QoGlpzOHI

Here’s our interview with Alex Albon about a grim weekend at Monza.

“Alex Albon remembers the 2022 Italian Grand Prix well. He had been looking forward to it. ‘We had a car which was good down the straights that year so I was quite excited to be going to Monza,” the Williams driver recalls, a little wistfully.

‘We did FP1 and FP2 and sure enough we were quick so I was like: ‘This is going to be a good weekend.’

“Albon could not have been more wrong. He remembers waking at around 1am that night and being unable to get back to sleep.

“What happened next was the stuff of nightmares. Albon called the doctor, was diagnosed with appendicitis, sent to San Gerardo Hospital in Monza for surgery, only to suffer an unexpected complication during the procedure, which resulted in acute respiratory failure.”

He shares the joint record with Michael Schumacher for most wins at Monza.

Schumacher, a Ferrari legend, ended his career with five. Hamilton has the same.

Sport loves an emotional link to records, so be prepared for this to become a big moment.

Five wins apiece for Michael and Lewis 🖐#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/j10lMygYft

The Italian team are bringing an upgrade engine to Monza for the weekend.

Hamilton would desperately love to go out at the top after what is a remarkable return to decent form after some years of desperate struggle.

With Antonelli possibly out of the running this weekend, this is the chance to change the - *spits in self-scorn* - narrative.

Russell might have incurred a penalty if he had done this in qualifying.

The Mercedes man blocked Oscar Piastri’s run at a corner, forcing some heavy braking from his rival.

Thankfully, Piastri ducked out, and thankfully for Russell, he’s not facing censure.

Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton go racing! 🍿 pic.twitter.com/Zs8u8h4XoT

The former world champion is still looking for more from his car.

“The tow is everything here so [I’m] likely to be looking for the tow.”

Because Antonelli exceeded the limit of parts used for his engine, he is taking a grid penalty at Monza.

Few would entirely rule out a storming ride for him on Sunday to end up top of the pack, but is is clearly a huge task for him to score points of any kind with that disadvantage.

They are now likely both past their peaks, but Hamilton and Verstappen recalled their battles of 2021 when they clashed in practice earlier.

Verstappen was already hacked off with Hamilton for seemingly obstructing his path earlier in the session, and they almost came together in the dying moments of the session.

Hamilton needed to take the escape road at the first chicane, where the pair made contact in 2021, as Verstappen looked to slip around his occasional rival. The two of them scarcely avoided another contact.

On the radios, Verstappen claimed, “He caused that,” while Hamilton reported to Ferrari that he was, “Blocked by Max.” Perhaps there will be more aggro later.

FP3 CLASSIFICATIONRussell in the box seat heading into qualifying#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/BUrCsv92dT

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of and qualifying for the Monza Grand Prix.

Before the weekend’s racing, George Russell was, at least publicly, less than bullish about his chances in Italy.

He did, though, believe he would deliver a better showing than he had in recent weeks.

“I don’t know if we can say we’re favourites this weekend, but we probably have a greater opportunity than we’ve had in the last two races where it’s been less about the power unit and more about the chassis,” he said.

“It’s so close right now, that last tenth in qualifying can be the difference of a couple of positions, which can change the podium. Right now, I don’t know who is going to be the team to beat.”

Russell was almost a minute off winner Lando Norris of McLaren in Hungary, finishing seventh in his Mercedes. Two weeks ago, in the Netherlands, he took the last spot on the podium, with Norris winning again.

However, in the second practice session on Friday and FP3 today, Russell was quickest. He led his former colleague, Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton, who was second fastest.

Red Bull’s Max Verstappen hinted at a rare good weekend as he was third fastest, about a third of a second behind Russell.

Russell, of course, needs a win soon, or he is in danger of seeing the championship run away from him entirely, as Kimi Antonelli already leads him by 59 points in the world title chase.

Perhaps psychologically just as pressing is that erstwhile teammate Hamilton is tied with Russell on 183 points, in third because he has one victory compared to Russell’s two. Slipping down the rankings could knock his confidence.

Russell has not secured pole for the last four races, so a strong showing in qualifying might be the boost he needs ahead of Sunday’s race, while Norris is looking for a pole position hat-trick.

#2072. It pushes you forward – Jacob Murrell feeling fuelled by Falkirk fan fervour

Falkirk striker Jacob Murrell believes the passion of Scottish football is fuelling his goalscoring form.

The American has netted five goals since joining from DC United, helping the Bairns go on a four-game winning run ahead of Sunday’s trip to face Hearts.

The 22-year-old said: “It’s a little different just because the games matter a bit more here than they did back in the MLS, just because of the promotion/relegation and how much the fans care about results. So the intensity of the games is much higher, you’re not finding easy games.

“For me, it’s the best thing in the world to play under this type of pressure. It just gives me a purpose, it gives me that fuel.

“I love that aspect of it. I love that the way that our group goes on the field and performs matters to people. That’s the most special thing about what we get to do and it drives us on the hard days when we have to come to training, when we’re tired, when we’re sore.

Mika Baur identifies the Celtic challenge he is ready to rise to Neil McCann: Why nothing has changed in my approach to build strong Kilmarnock team

"We’re playing for something more than ourselves, that pushes you forward.

Murrell was among 17 summer signings but manager John McGlynn has quickly fashioned the group into an effective team.

“The people have been really good to me,” he said. “Falkirk in general has been really good to me. The club, the team-mates, but then the fans as well have been really good.

“There’s a bit of learning curve the first month to get up to speed and get all the stuff sorted with a car, an apartment and a bank account. All the stuff that you don’t see behind the scenes.

“Little stuff that’s different, like when I went to the grocery store, I couldn’t find eggs. Back home, they’re only in the fridge. They’re on the shelf here.

“But I’ve got into a really good rhythm with a couple of team-mates going to the gym after training and just getting into good habits where we’re cooking our own food and eating well.

“Just feeling full of confidence that we’re putting in the work and we’re going to reap the benefits of it.”

#2071. Leeds United vs Tottenham Hotspur - prediction, team news, lineups

By Oliver Thomas | 05 Nov 2026 16:00, Last updated: 07 Nov 2026 11:06

A resurgent Tottenham Hotspur side travel to Elland Road to take on an out-of-sorts Leeds United outfit in the Premier League on Saturday lunchtime.

The spoils were shared the last time these two teams butted heads in May, with Mathys Tel’s opener cancelled out by a Dominic Calvert-Lewin penalty to rescue a 1-1 draw in North London.

After making a bright start to the season, accumulating eight points from their opening four games (W2 D2), Leeds are now without a win across their last five matches (D3 L2) and have slipped down to 12th in the Premier League table.

The Whites continue to stumble after a 2-0 defeat against Bournemouth, adding to a rough patch that includes a 2-1 loss at champions Arsenal alongside draws with struggling trio Crystal Palace, Manchester United and Sunderland.

Head coach Daniel Farke – who reached an agreement in principle over a contract extension last month – has downplayed concerns over Leeds' recent winless streak, maintaining that his squad remains calm and confident while prioritising reaching the 40-point safety mark as quickly as possible.

Leeds should welcome a return to Elland Road where they are unbeaten across their last eight league matches (W4 D4); they are one of only four Premier League teams yet to lose on home soil so far this season along with Arsenal, Brighton and Hull.

However, the Whites have collected only five points across their last 13 top-flight battles with Spurs, losing 10 of those, while they have failed to keep a clean sheet in any of their last 16 encounters with the North Londoners – a 1-0 home win back in February 2000 was the last time Leeds did not concede against Spurs.

After enduring a six-game winless start to the Premier League, Tottenham’s early-season struggles now seem to be behind them as Roberto De Zerbi has steered his team to three consecutive victories against Coventry, Chelsea and Crystal Palace.

Spurs opened their account with a 3-1 home win over Coventry just under a fortnight ago and have since recorded back-to-back 2-0 successes against Chelsea and Palace, beating the latter last weekend after taking advantage of a 13th-minute red card for Eagles striker Jean-Philippe Mateta.

The North Londoners have risen up to ninth place in the Premier League table, just two points behind the top five and crucially five points clear of the bottom three; they are now bidding to win four league games in a row for the first time since September and October 2023.

De Zerbi has encouraged his players to build on their positive upturn in form, as three straight wins is “not enough” to please the supporters. The Italian also hopes to see a ‘nastier’ side from his attacking players in front of goal after scoring only two goals from 34 shots against Palace.

Spurs head into Saturday’s contest with Leeds seeking to extend their three-game unbeaten away run in the top flight, while they have won each of their last three visits to Elland Road by an aggregate score of 10-2.

Tottenham Hotspur form (all competitions):

Leeds duo Noah Okafor (adductor) and Anton Stach (broken toe) remain major doubts, while Farke "carefully optimistic" that striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin – who has scored seven goals in his last seven home games – will be fit after missing training on Thursday with a foot problem.

Former Spurs defender Joe Rodon is back in full training and in contention to return to the matchday squad after missing the last eight games in all competitions with a hamstring injury. A start is considered unlikely, though, so James Justin, Nico Elvedi and Tarik Muharemovic should all continue in the back three.

James Trafford will "remain in goal" despite his costly mistake in the defeat at Bournemouth, while Lukas Nmecha, Brenden Aaronson and Jean-Matteo Bahoya are three attackers who could be considered for a start should Farke look to shake up his attack.

As for Tottenham, Savio (muscle), Lucas Bergvall, Wilson Odobert (both knee), Mykhaylo Mudryk (ankle) and Xavi Simons (ACL) all remain out, though the latter is making positive progress in his recovery and could return soon than expected.

However, Tosin Adarabioyo has recovered from a calf injury and Rodrigo Bentancur is also available after serving a three-match suspension.

De Zerbi may look to make only two changes to his starting lineup, with Pedro Porro pushing to replace Archie Gray at right-back, while playmaker James Maddison could start at the expense of either Omar Marmoush or Dominic Solanke who are both battling for the centre-forward spot.

Trafford; Justin, Elvedi, Muharemovic; Bogle, Ampadu, Tanaka, Gudmundsson; Wilson, James; Calvert-Lewin

Tottenham Hotspur possible starting lineup:

Kinsky; Porro, Van Hecke, Van de Ven, Robertson; Fernandes, Tonali; Kudus, Maddison, Tel, Solanke

Seven of Leeds’ nine Premier League matches this season have produced under 2.5 goals and we expected another tight affair against Tottenham this weekend.

The momentum is certainly with Spurs right now, but Leeds have made themselves difficult to beat at Elland Road and we can envisage the spoils being shared in a low-scoring draw on this occasion.

#2061. Tottenham lineup vs. Leeds: Predicted XI for Premier League clash

By Oliver Thomas | 05 Nov 2026 16:05, Last updated: 06 Nov 2026 16:04

Tottenham Hotspur will be without five players for Saturday’s Premier League clash with Leeds United at Elland Road.

Xavi Simons is believed to be making positive progress in his recovery from an ACL injury and could return soon than anticipated. However, an appearance against Leeds is not on the cards.

Savio (muscle), Lucas Bergvall, Wilson Odobert (both knee) and Mykhaylo Mudryk (ankle) also remain out injuried, but Tosin Adarabioyo is available having recovered from a calf issue, while Rodrigo Bentancur is back from a three-game ban.

Head coach Roberto De Zerbi is not expected to make wholesale changes to a side that won their third Premier League game in a row last weekend, beating Crystal Palace 2-0 on home soil.

However, Pedro Porro is a strong contender to return at right-back at the expense of Arche Gray, potentially joining Jan Paul van Hecke, Micky van de Ven and Andrew Robertson in a four-man defence.

While Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes are set to continue their central midfield partnership, playmaker James Maddison could be recalled to play an advanced role after watching on as an unused substitute against Palace.

The potential return of Maddison could see Omar Marmoush drop down to the substitutes’ bench, with Mohammed Kudus, Mathys Tel and Dominic Solanke all linking up in a three-man frontline.

Tottenham Hotspur possible starting lineup:

Kinsky; Porro, Van Hecke, Van de Ven, Robertson; Fernandes, Tonali; Kudus, Maddison, Tel, Solanke

#2059. Newcastle’s limitations exposed by Bournemouth before hosts fight back for draw

This was the definition of a hard-earned point. Newcastle United came back from two goals down to rescue a point against Bournemouth, but this was not a convincing performance from Matthias Jaissle’s side.

Newcastle were abject for the first half an hour and the visitors could have been out of sight. It was disjointed and lacklustre as Bournemouth dominated before the break and regularly threatened Lukasz Hornicek in goal.

Even during the fightback, Newcastle lacked cohesion and penetration, but forced their way back into it through hard work, spirit and determination. Whether you believe Harvey Barnes’ wonder goal and Jacob Ramsey’s late strike paper over the cracks or reveal a togetherness – a grit and determination that bodes well for the future – depends on the individual.

Ramsey comes off the bench to fire Newcastle level! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UBWAfCQyy4

For the second weekend in a row, Newcastle had just two shots on target and scored two goals. At the other end of the pitch, they have allowed their opponents 61 shots in just three games, the highest in the division. That is not going to be sustainable long term. Something Jaissle acknowledged.

“It shows where we have potential,” he said. “There are elements to improve offensively.

“The learning curve is there. There were some elements missing from our performance but there was a strong response. The lads showed big character, big personality and big commitment... It is always better to get a point and see the potential to improve.”

A reality check is not necessarily a bad thing. There has been a lot of hype and excitement on Tyneside and a self-congratulating tone to their own end of summer appraisals.

But this was a reminder of the team’s limitations and the fact that only three of their eight summer signings started the game, with two more coming off the bench, underlined they are a work in progress.

In truth, that is fine. It is the start of September and the Premier League campaign is only three games old. They have a new manager and a new-look team. There has been a significant amount of change in a very short period of time.

It was not the easiest summer, and despite the insistence from senior figures at the club that they had always remained calm and methodical during their summer reset, there was a whiff of crisis only a few weeks ago.

When Eddie Howe quit as manager and Bruno Guimarães, the captain, forced his move to Arsenal at the start of August, Newcastle looked in disarray. So, to have started the season unbeaten from three games against Liverpool, Tottenham Hotspur and Bournemouth is encouraging.

It is also worth highlighting just how good the visitors were. In the first half Bournemouth were superb, rushing Newcastle, forcing mistakes and pouring forward in numbers. In Alex Scott, just as he was in their victory here last season, Bournemouth had the best player on the pitch.

That opens up another conversation. Newcastle played like this a lot at home in Howe’s final season in charge, especially in the second-half of the campaign, but tended to lose not draw the game.

On this occasion, they secured a decent point with a late equaliser thanks to substitute Ramsey, who looked good when he replaced the off-colour Lewis Miley.

Bournemouth will feel they should have held on. They had taken a deserved lead through Marcus Tavernier, who took advantage of a static and ball-watching Amar Dedić to bundle home from close range.

Tavernier gives Bournemouth the lead at St James' Park! 🍒🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/mDdb5uV4hj

Marco Rose’s side should have scored again minutes later when Sven Botman gifted the ball to Evanilson on the edge of the Newcastle area, but he failed to hit the target.

Bournemouth had their tails up and when another blunder from Dedic – galloping forward and losing possession with a heavy touch – Nico González, another new signing, failed to make a tackle to stop the attack.

Justin Kluivert’s long-range strike thumped against the post and hit the back of goalkeeper Lukasz Hornicek. Scott reacted quickest and his cross spun into his own net off the leg of Malick Thiaw.

Bournemouth have a second and St James' Park is stunned! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Kyy91awf39

Newcastle were in disarray and were lucky to be back in the game before half-time as Barnes whipped in a stunning strike 25 seconds after the restart.

Bournemouth have a second and St James' Park is stunned! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Kyy91awf39

Despite seeing more of the ball, other than a Joe Willock header that dropped wide of the post early in the second half, Newcastle did not create another clear goal-scoring opportunity until Ramsey’s equaliser.

That is a cause for concern, but Newcastle remain unbeaten. Nothing shapes perceptions more than results. Jaissle is right to cling to the positives from that.

Speaking to TNT Sports, the Newcastle boss said: “Mixed feelings. Happy for that spirit, that belief the lads were showing until the end together with the crowd. I felt the energy and felt if we had five or 10 minutes more we could win this game. But the first half was not expected. This is something we need to improve. This is part of the journey.

“We knew Bournemouth would come with everything, they always show great intensity and if you do not compete with that you get problems. We struggled with that in the first half but the lads showed the right reaction.”

"I'm really happy with the confidence the lads brought onto the pitch today." 👏Marco Rose reflects on Bournemouth's performance after taking a point at St James' Park.🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/GULqEAUSbx

It’s all over at St James’ Park. Newcastle come from two goals down to salvage a hard-fought point against Bournemouth. A thrilling first half comes to a close. What a fantastic game of football so far. Bournemouth flew into a two-goal lead through Tavernier’s composed finish and Thiaw’s own goal, before Newcastle pulled one back thanks to Barnes’ superb strike. Oh dear not a great moment for two of Newcastle’s summer signings as Bournemouth extend their lead. Amar Dedic lost the ball with a heavy touch and Nico Gonzalez’s half hearted tackle failed to halt Bournenouth’s counter attack.

An unchanged line up for Newcastle United in Matthias Jaissle’s third Premier League game as manager but this is a very different sort of challenge.

These are the fixtures Eddie Howe’s team repeatedly slipped up in at home last season, where the likes of Everton, Brentford, Bournemouth and Sunderland all won.

Can Jaissle improve that record? Can his team thrive when they are likely to have more of the ball, play against a low block defence and an opponent adept at lightning-fast counterattacks?

Does the German’s “vertical” football have as much success against a team that does not play a high defensive line as Liverpool and Tottenham did?

We are likely to know a lot more about Newcastle after this game. There has been a lot of hype and excitement after an impressive start to the new season but have people got a little carried away?

Let’s see how they get on against a Bournemouth side that probably should have got at least a point away to Manchester City in their opening away game.

Good morning and welcome to our live coverage of this Saturday lunchtime fixture between Newcastle United and Bournemouth at St James’ Park.

The hosts have made a determined start to the 2025-26 season under new head coach Matthias Jaissle. They conceded a last-minute penalty to draw 2-2 with Liverpool on the opening weekend of the Premier League campaign, sealed a hard-fought 3-2 victory over West Bromwich Albion in the Carabao Cup, and then produced an inspired second-half performance to win 2-0 away at Tottenham in their previous top-flight outing.

Despite anxiety in the summer after losing Eddie Howe and multiple key players such as Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimaraes and Anthony Gordon, the Jaissle era has begun very encouragingly. New signings including Lukas Hornicek, Amar Dedic and Nico Gonzalez have seamlessly slotted into the starting XI, Lewis Hall has been typically brilliant, while Anthony Elanga and Yoane Wissa look reborn up top after both forwards endured difficult campaigns last season.

Marco Rose’s Bournemouth tenure has started in frustrating circumstances. They had been leading 1-0 against Manchester City in their first top-flight fixture this campaign, but conceded two late goals to dramatically lose 2-1. Bournemouth were also left kicking themselves last weekend against Everton, after a defensive mix-up between Ryan Christie and Marcus Tavernier following a corner delivery gifted James Tarkowski a 91st-minute equaliser, allowing the visitors to salvage a 1-1 draw at the Vitality Stadium.

At opposite ends of the country, over 350 miles separate these two sides. Away days in English football can’t really get any longer. The travelling Bournemouth support will hope their loyalty can be repaid with a first Premier League win of the season under Rose, while Newcastle will aim to continue their unbeaten start and carry on the positive momentum created by Jaissle.

Kick-off is at 12:30, with team news coming shortly.

#2058. ‘They deserve it’ – Kostas Tsimikas admits familiar failing cost Liverpool in Istanbul

Kostas Tsimikas admitted that Liverpool got what they deserved in their 3-2 defeat to Fenerbahce in Istanbul on Wednesday.

The Reds were in front twice at the Sukru Saracoglu Stadium but still contrived to come away with nothing against Dirk Kuyt’s side, who claimed all three points thanks to Vedat Muriqi’s 79th-minute header.

Jeremy Jacquet was criticised for turning his back on Mason Greenwood’s free kick for the first equaliser, and Alisson Becker was culpable of poor positioning for Archie Brown’s goal to make it 2-2.

Speaking to UEFA.com after the match, Tsimikas magnanimously conceded that Fenerbahce were full value for their win and lamented Liverpool’s defending over the goals that they shipped.

The Greek defender said (via BBC Sport): “Congratulations to Fenerbahce, they deserve it. We didn’t play how we had to play. We didn’t defend after the goal we conceded. After three or four minutes, automatically we conceded another goal.

“I think we have to mark better if we want to win games. We didn’t play very good and that’s why we lost.”

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

It sums up how careless Liverpool were this evening that they were in the lead twice and occupied a winning position for only eight minutes against Fenerbahce, with the goals from Trey Nyoni and Alexander Isak cancelled out all too quickly.

The manner of all three goals that the home side scored will enrage Iraola – it wasn’t as though the Istanbul outfit had to produce moments of magic to inspire their way to victory over the Reds.

Tsimikas himself was far from convincing, enduring a ‘tough night’ in the words of Liverpool Echo reporter Paul Gorst as he struggled to contain the threat of Greenwood, and he ended up being substituted for Milos Kerkez with 15 minutes remaining.

Liverpool have now conceded 10 goals in their four Champions League matches, shipping three for the third European fixture in a row, a record which’ll surely concern the head coach at this phase of the competition.

The debrief from this game will not be a pleasant one, and a much better defensive performance will be required if the Reds are to return to winning ways against Crystal Palace on Sunday.

#2057. Celtic's 'Che Guevaras' should show their fellow fans some respect at this year's AGM

There is about as much chance of Dermot Desmond taking a seat amongst the Union Bears ultras group the next time Celtic play Rangers at Ibrox in January as there is of the billionaire Irish financier rocking up at their AGM at Parkhead next month.

Desmond, who has been the Glasgow club’s principal shareholder for more than two decades, has not attended the gathering since way back in 2006 and he is not, with disaffection about the stewardship of the Scottish champions still rife in the stands, about to break with tradition.

The greeting which chief executive Michael Nicholson, chief financial officer Chris McKay, interim chairman Brian Wilson and manager Martin O’Neill received from some protesters when they attended a question-and-answer session at the Greenock Supporters’ Club this week gave an indication of the sort of treatment he would receive if he did.

Speaking at his pre-match press conference ahead of the Europa League encounter with Besiktas on Thursday night, O’Neill expressed his dismay at the fact that around 25 supporters appeared wearing face coverings. “That was the saddest thing,” he said. “I would never have thought that fans would be clothed in balaclavas at a meeting.”

The frustration in the statement which the Celtic Fans Collective, an umbrella coalition of supporters’ clubs and organisations, published this week demanding that Desmond make a rare appearance at the meeting was palpable and understandable.

That the man who, rightly or wrongly but unquestionably, wields the most power at Parkhead is an annual no-show highlights everything that is wrong with how the former European Cup winners are being run. Are accountability and dialogue too much to ask for?

Is the famously publicity-shy man from Macroom in County Cork, though, really going to trap when the same individuals who hurled tennis balls at him when he was playing golf in the Alfred Dunhill Championship at St Andrews last month are likely to be in attendance?

There has been fevered speculation about when Celtic directors will face their shareholders in recent weeks. Supporters are desperate to know what their long-term football strategy is, who has been driving recruitment, how governance is going to be modernised, why tens of millions of pounds continue to sit in the bank and much else besides.

But are they likely to get answers to those questions now the AGM date has been set for Tuesday, December 1? The actions of a certain sub-section of their support in Inverclyde in midweek suggested that it could well be another bad-tempered, ugly and ultimately futile get-together.

Celtic interim chairman Brian Wilson, left, chief executive Michael Nicholson and chief financial officer Chris McKay at Parkhead (Image: Stuart Wallace / Shutterstock)

Ill-feeling about then-chairman Peter Lawwell bringing last year's annual meeting to a premature end amid persistent disorder still lingers. It has been suggested once again in recent days that the move was a cynical ploy by the besieged board to avoid public scrutiny.

However, David Low, the financial analyst who was a driving force behind the Fergus McCann takeover back in 1994 and is now associated with the Celtic Supporters Limited pressure group, rejected that interpretation of events when he appeared on the A Celtic State of Mind podcast last week.

“You are allowed to hold the people who shareholders elected to account once a year,” he said. “But it is a professional environment. Last year’s meeting was a bun fight. Nobody came out of that looking well. It is a professional forum and you have to respect the forum you are in.

“Give them red cards if you have to if they give an unsatisfactory answer. But listen to what is said and then react. That is the way it has always been at Celtic, even when it was a private company.

“That was a horrible meeting last year. People go there who want to learn. That is why they are there. You turn up, you ask questions and you try to learn something. If you don’t like it you can boo and do whatever within reason. But you have got to listen.

“It disintegrated into a shambles last year. It was over-the-top. There was a lot of unacceptable behaviour from the hardcore. It was not on. It was the biggest AGM in 20 years.”

There has been widespread unhappiness about the course Celtic are on for some time and a substantial section of the support wants meaningful change in how the Parkhead club is run. But some of the more vocal and militant members of the rebel alliance can be arrogant and selfish.

They did not merely show disrespect to the board last year. They showed disrespect to the hundreds of fellow shareholders who had turned up, many from far afield, wanting to exercise the same right to scrutinise those running their club.

The club later alleged that its head of safety, security and operations, Mark Hargreaves, had been threatened and intimidated by two prominent members of the Green Brigade. Whatever the truth of those allegations, it was a sorry affair from start to premature finish.

Celtic fans hold up banners referencing their teams failures against teams in Europe (Image: Andrew Milligan)

One lifelong fan voiced his exasperation at the leaders of the civil war that was raging at his beloved club in these pages as he attended the Scottish Gas Scottish Cup game against Dundee back in February.

“We don't need modern-day Che Guevaras,” he said before he ignored the boycott that had been called. “We want people who love Celtic.” He is not alone in taking that view.

The Celtic Fans Collective appealed for the “focus to be firmly on scrutiny rather than protest” at the AGM in their latest missive. They are right. The board should be made to answer searching questions. Those who shout directors down before their answers can be heard are serving neither their cause nor their fellow supporters.

It would perhaps help the Parkhead club to move forward on and off the park if those words were heeded and there were no disruptions from “aggressive and irrational factions” hellbent on “stirring up toxicity”.

#2048. The Celtic 'rollercoaster' Mika Baur is getting used to & how he spends his days off

It is easy to forget that Mika Baur only turned 22 over the summer. The German midfielder displayed maturity beyond his years in Celtic's captivating Europa League victory over Besiktas on Thursday evening, chasing lost causes, contributing defensively, and progressing play forward when the opportunity arrived.

It was his finest performance since joining the club for an initial fee of £4.5 million from Paderborn in August.

Baur compared his first few months in Glasgow to riding a rollercoaster, with downtime away from the football pitch proving rare.

"There’s no time to think about it! We are playing every three days and I really try to fight and bring my heart on the field all the time," Baur said. "Sometimes it works, sometimes it doesn’t, but I hope people understand as a young player it can be tough to be comfortable in a new country, a new culture and new club.

"But I really try my best. I have felt good in my first few months but it is a bit of a rollercoaster.

"Playing in this unbelievable stadium in front of these fans, getting the call-up to the national team was a big honour. You feel the pressure with some of the games we have lost but I am getting used to it."

This is Baur's first time living away from home. He credits his partner for making the transition to Scotland smoother, even if chances to play some golf are limited.

"I’m grateful to my girlfriend as she does most things and makes it comfortable at home," Baur continued. "The club also have people who have helped us a lot to settle.

"But you don’t get much time – you get home and lie on the couch!

"It’s not all stressful though. It’s also nice to go somewhere new and learn the city, get to coffee shops and restaurants.

"We’ve been to the beach, we’ve been to Edinburgh, we try to see a lot on our day off.

"I also play golf – so I’ve come to the home of golf! I’ve only managed to get to the driving range though. When you are playing every three days it’s a bit much to play nine or 18 holes.

"My father and brother play so hopefully the weather will be okay around Christmas to maybe manage a few holes."

Thursday's win over Besiktas wasn't quite a hole-in-one, but it marked a pivotal forward step in Celtic's Europa League campaign.

Finally up and running after consecutive defeats to Ferencvaros, Benfica and Celta Vigo, Baur gave credit to a raucous home support.

"The fans helped a lot," he explained. "You could feel the energy. It was not just us players on the field who deserved the win – it was also everyone around the stadium and they brought the energy as well.

"It’s an unbelievable feeling as a player to have everyone pushing you and being there for you. It gives you that last percentage of energy you need at the end.

"There is always pressure to win here, to win every three days. That’s what we all want. In the last two games it wasn’t possible for us. We knew it wasn’t good enough but here we played well and deserved it."

"The win was important after some tough weeks," Baur continued. "But the belief and the way we work together as a team has always been good.

"There was never any problem with that because we always believed in ourselves. We showed how we can leave our hearts on the field and put in a shift.

"It was important to get those three points and we deserved it. Hopefully we can go forward with confidence from this game."

Despite his stellar showing on Thursday, Baur missed out on Jurgen Klopp's latest Germany squad. He made his senior international debut against Serbia last month as the former Liverpool manager had named two separate squads for four fixtures.

Klopp's group was reduced this time around, though Baur will return to the under-21s.

"I can understand," Baur said of the snub. "There are so many unbelievable players in the squad, especially in my position.

"We’re talking about guys from Bayern Munich and Borussia Dortmund. I just do my best and hopefully they can see I am developing and improving.

"I’m still with the under-21s for the games against Belgium and Croatia, so that will be good. European matches like Thursday can only help and I have to hope they see.

"I’m still young but I’ll keep doing my best and we’ll see what happens next time."

#2046. Next Man United manager: Special Cesc Fabregas agreement truth 'revealed' amid Red Devils struggle

By Carter White | 05 Nov 2026 16:50, Last updated: 05 Nov 2026 20:51

Como president Miran Suwarso has denied the presence of a special clause in Cesc Fabregas's managerial contract.

Manchester United fans are watching the 39-year-old's coaching work with considerable envy at the beginning of this term, with the Red Devils supposedly reaching out to Didier Deschamps over potentially replacing Michael Carrick.

It is not only the dugout where the 20-time English champions are plotting change, with Man Utd keen to improve their defensive ranks in the New Year, leading to a supposed interest in Fulham and Nigeria centre-back Calvin Bassey.

Winning just one of their opening nine top-flight fixtures, Carrick's side are sitting in a lowly 17th position in the Premier League standings, lying outside of the division's relegation zone on goal difference.

Fabregas's up-and-coming Como outfit embarrassed Man Utd in the Champions League on October 21, when Argentinian ace Nico Paz bagged a brace in a 4-1 battering of the Red Devils in the League Phase.

Appearing on Piers Morgan Uncensored, Como president Suwarso discussed the future of head coach Fabregas, who has understandably attracted plenty of interest from other European clubs.

Reports in September suggested that the 39-year-old had a 'special agreement' in his contract that would allow him to depart the Serie A club to join three of his former sides - Barcelona, Arsenal or Chelsea - for a fixed compensation fee.

Como chief Suwarso has rubbished those rumours, saying: "He does not need a clause to go anywhere he wants. In a business like this, he is a friend more than anything else.

"He can go wherever he wants, whenever he wants. I could even say if tomorrow, he calls me and he says, 'Hey, I want to go to [Bayer] Leverkusen', for example. I would say, 'If that is something you want to do, then go'. I don't even need any compensation."

Fabregas's current contract at Como expires during the summer of 2028, before which intrigue in the young Spanish tactician is undoubtedly set to grow exponentially, including from clubs in the Premier League.

Given that it is down to Fabregas to decide the timing of his exit from Como, it is extremely unlikely that struggling Manchester United will be getting their claws on the Spaniard anytime soon.

The former Gunners midfielder is building something special at the Serie A newcomers, who could be the surprise package of the Champions League this term, following in the footsteps of Norwegian side Bodo/Glimt during 2025-26.

Man Utd are mess from the boardroom to the pitch at the moment, and nothing but the club's proud history stands above their competitors at present, leaving the Old Trafford faithful in relative misery.

#2045. Bayern were ready to pay £58.3m for Rio Ngumoha & may test Liverpool again

Rio Ngumoha’s future at Liverpool could be under threat next summer.

That’s because Bayern Munich reportedly remain ‘in talks’ with the young Englishman’s camp following a failed push to sign the winger this year.

Christian Falk reports for CF Bayern Insider that FC Bayern were prepared to put their money where their mouth is for the teenager in the summer.

A figure to the tune of €70m [£58.3m] was discussed, however, Liverpool’s uncompromising position on the matter meant that an alternative avenue in Ismael Saibari was instead prioritised.

“It is TRUE: Bayern Munich were prepared to pay €70m [£58.3m] for Rio Ngumoha. As we know, Bayern have been searching really hard for options on the left wing,” the head of sport at BILD said.

“We talked about Bradley Barcola, whom they were in contact with, and they were also in contact with Liverpool’s young talent. There were talks, his brother talked with FC Bayern, but it was a difficult situation for Bayern Munich. It was not clear if Liverpool would sell him or not. The price wouldn’t have been extremely high.

You’d have to think Andoni Iraola and Co. will be pretty comfortable despite interest from abroad in Ngumoha’s services.

But if the ultimate goal is development and access to a pathway, he’s clearly already got that at Liverpool.

#2044. The town of Clydebank knows all about triumphs and traumas. Now a little Blitz spirit is helping their defiant football team rise to prominence once again

Published: 12:23 EDT, 2 November 2026 | Updated: 12:48 EDT, 2 November 2026

Five framed photographs hang on the walls of the clubhouse lounge at Holm Park: the Titan crane, the Singer sewing factory and Kilbowie Park, as well as the rubble-strewn streets of the Blitz and the long-lost Seven Seas pub. Together, they tell the story of a town, its triumphs and its traumas.

‘There’s an old Bankies song,’ says Clydebank FC chair Grace McGibbon, who had the pictures installed at the start of this season. ‘It goes, “We make ships, sewing machines, we build famous football teams, we’re the Bankies from Kilbowie Park”. It’s kind of a homage to that.’

To McGibbon, the pictures are a reminder of what Clydebank is and has always been.

‘Clydebank is not just a football team, or a shopping centre, or whatever else you might think,’ she tells Daily Mail Sport. ‘It’s so much more than any of that. This is a community that never gives up. There’s almost a defiance about the place. That’s what these photos represent.

‘Other people might look at it and go, “It’s just pictures on a wall, I don’t get it”. But we get it. It reminds us why we’re here and why we’re doing this.’

Without question, ‘this’ is one of the Scottish football stories of the season so far. As well as being in contention for the Lowland League West title – and with it, the chance of a Lazarus-like return to the Scottish football league – Clydebank have reached the third round of the Scottish Cup for the third successive season where Championship side Livingston await.

Clydebank finished top of a KDM Evolution Trophy league phase containing mainly senior sides

More immediately, they host League One strugglers Alloa Athletic in the last 32 of the KDM Evolution Trophy on Tuesday, the Bankies having qualified for the knockout stages of the Challenge Cup by finishing top of the league phase, unbeaten, and ahead of the likes of Ross County, Airdrieonians and Cove Rangers.

Be under no illusions: something special is happening in West Dunbartonshire just now. To fully understand how special requires a short history lesson. Between 1888 and 1931, three clubs bearing the Clydebank name came and went. It was in the 1960s that things changed materially.

Frustrated by poor attendances, and inspired by Major League Baseball franchise relocations, Jack and Charlie Steedman – the majority owners of East Stirlingshire FC – merged their club with Clydebank Juniors. ES Clydebank, as they were called, relocated to New Kilbowie Park in Clydebank, enraging supporters of the hitherto Falkirk-based East Stirlingshire.

A legal challenge brought by local shareholders saw the merger invalidated and the brothers being deposed. Undeterred, they formed a brand-new club, Clydebank FC, which successfully applied for entry into the Scottish football league in time for the 1966/67 season. A decade later, inspired by a 20-year-old Davie Cooper, the club was promoted to the Premier Division for the first time, narrowly missing out on the First Division title to Alex Ferguson’s St Mirren.

For a while, everything was gravy. The Bankies established themselves as a solid if unspectacular outfit, represented at various times by the likes of Owen Coyle, Tommy Coyne and Bobby Williamson. The ‘two Jims’, Fallon and Gallacher, became club icons alongside record-goalscorer Ken Eadie. Gary Teale rose through the club’s youth academy. They even lured Cooper home to see out his career.

Kilbowie Park was one of the iconic stops for away fans before it was razed to the ground

In 1996, the rug was pulled. The Steedmans sold New Kilbowie Park to developers who demolished the ground and built a retail park on top of it. That sparked a chain of events that included ground-sharing with Dumbarton and Greenock Morton, ownership changes, and ill-conceived plans to relocate to Dublin, then Carlisle, the Scottish Borders and more.

After the inevitable tumble into administration, the club was acquired by the newly formed Airdrie United, itself a product of the liquidated Airdrieonians. To all intents and purposes, Clydebank FC was renamed and relocated, leaving devastated Bankies without a club.

McGibbon remembers it well. ‘I’m Clydebank born and bred,’ she beams. ‘My husband had been a Clydebank fan all his days and, when we first met, he took me along to a couple of games. I immediately got the bug.

‘So, when the demise happened, you felt it. This thing that was so important to you was suddenly gone. It was heartbreaking. The season after it happened, you’d bump into people wandering around the shopping centre because that was the only place left to go.’

As Scottish football carried on without them, a group of fans formed a collective called the United Clydebank Supporters and recovered the club name and crest from Airdrie United. ‘At that point,’ recalls McGibbon, ‘we basically had to take a crash course in how to run a football club. People talk about starting again from scratch. That’s what this was. Absolute scratch.’

Scottish football icon Davie Cooper started and finished his playing career with the Bankies

Item one on the agenda was an application to join the Scottish Junior Football League. After that was accepted, and after a year out of the game, Clydebank returned in time for the start of the 2003-04 campaign. Club legend Billy ‘Budgie’ McGhee was named manager, a new home at Glenhead Park in Duntocher was secured, and an improbable new chapter began.

Fast-forward roughly a quarter of a century, and the progress made is quite remarkable. Via various rungs of the former Scottish Junior Football Association and ground-hopping arrangements, Clydebank joined the West of Scotland League – the sixth tier of the Scottish football pyramid – in 2020. In 2024-25, they won promotion to the Lowland League West to move to within a step of a sensational return to the Scottish football league.

Win the league and they will go into a three-way, end-of-season play-off with the champions of Lowland League East and the Highland League. The winner of that round-robin will advance to a two-legged, home-and-away play-off against the team finishing bottom of SPFL League Two, sometimes referred to as ‘Club 42’. Win that tie and you’re playing League Two football next season.

‘We have a three-year plan to be in League Two,’ says McGibbon. ‘Within five years, League One. And after that, who knows? The most important thing is that we remain sustainable and fan-owned.

‘We can’t sell out to a big money man. Do that and you sell the soul of the club. I know because we’ve been there before. We can never again be in a position where one person has sole ownership of this club. It just can’t happen.’

Which raises the question of governance. The ten-person board, chaired by McGibbon, is entirely voluntary. ‘We don’t take a penny out of the club,’ she insists. ‘No expenses, nothing.’

Pop group Wet Wet Wet sponsored their hometown club Clydebank between 1993 and 1997

Another 30 or so volunteers manage various other parts of club business, from running the social media accounts to curating the matchday programme to operating the club shop. If it feels as though the community is showing up for its team, that’s because it is.

‘I think it harks back to the town’s working-class roots,’ says McGibbon. ‘And we try to embrace it in kind. We understand that it’s difficult for people to buy season tickets and such like with the cost of everything these days. That’s why we’ve put things in place to help, like payment plans. If we know someone genuinely can’t afford a ticket, we try to make it happen. Sometimes, it’s more important to have that person there than bringing in an extra few quid on the day.’

Crucially, the club has also invested in the Bronze Licence required for promotion into the upper tiers of the pyramid, a significant outlay that has the full backing of manager Gordon Moffat.

‘The whole trajectory of the club is so positive,’ he says. ‘For me, my coaches and the players, it’s really reassuring to see the way the club is run. Grace and the board are basically lifelong fans and it’s obvious to anyone they’ve got the club’s long-term future at heart.

‘When I came in seven years ago, I said to Grace that we’d need to increase the playing budget if we wanted to be competitive and, to her credit, she’s managed to do that whilst keeping us on a sure footing. She’s not scared to say no but, at the same time, she’s a fan and she wants to watch a good team.’

Clydebank chair Grace McGibbon is proud of the way the club has battled through adversity

Currently, that team includes an eclectic mix of joiners, electricians, engineers, firefighters, a barber and more. There’s a potent mix of youth and experience, with leaders in every position. Nicky Low, for example. The former Aberdeen and Dundee midfielder joined the Bankies in February 2023, back when they were still in the West of Scotland Football League.

‘I knew a few boys who were there at the time,’ says the 34-year-old. ‘I said to them, “Listen, is it professional the way it’s run, because I’m not coming if it’s a bag of washing”. Honestly, they couldn’t have spoken more highly of the place, and they were right to.

‘It’s the volunteer aspect that really gets me. Clydebank’s lucky that a lot of people give up their free time to help out, and you see what it means to them when you win and they’re all high-fiving you. Just seeing people smiling at football is what makes it all worthwhile.’

For Low, playing for Clydebank also represents something of a ‘full circle’ moment. ‘I was brought up in Greenock,’ he says, ‘so when Clydebank were ground-sharing with Morton back in the day, I was their ball boy. I’ve had a soft spot for them since I was a kid.’

All of which is lovely but football – as we are constantly reminded – is a results business, and Low is determined to continue Clydebank’s momentum with a win over Alloa in the Challenge Cup.

‘We’re under no illusions about how difficult a game it’s going to be,’ he says. ‘Alloa are a strong team. They play good football and Andy Graham will have them well organised. They’ll be favourites but we’ll go in believing that if we can bring the best version of ourselves, we’ll have a chance of progressing.

Holm Park will play host to a cup clash against Alloa that could provide a real fairytale

‘As a team and as individuals, we’re playing well and we always believe we can score, so if we can keep it tight at the back, I believe we’re capable of giving anybody a game.’

Manager Moffat agrees. ‘We’ve shown against League One and League Two teams over the last few seasons that we can compete. People will say, “It’s a one-off game, anything can happen.” But we’ve got a decent sample size in our favour now. Sure, we’ll lose some games to SPFL opposition, but I think we’ve proven we’re more than capable of winning plenty, too.’

As for McGibbon, she’s mostly just happy to have her team back. ‘I work in retail,’ she says. ‘Monday to Thursday. Nothing exciting. My passion comes from this football club, from the people, the fans, the coaches, the players. Every single person at the club, I absolutely love them for what they’ve given. That’s what makes it all worthwhile. I mean, you wouldn’t do this if it didn’t mean something to you. But it does. It’s very special.’

And who knows? Maybe one day there will be space on the wall for a photo of the team that restores Clydebank to the Scottish football league. They, too, will have earned their place.

■ Clydebank FC face Alloa Athletic in the last 32 of the KDM Evolution Trophy at Holm Park on Tuesday, November 3. Kick-off 7.45pm.

#2043. How many points do Man Utd need in the Champions League?

By Naim Beneddra | 05 Nov 2026 17:01

Manchester United's dramatic comeback against Roma has revived their Champions League campaign, but Michael Carrick's side still have work to do to avoid an early European exit.

Tuesday's 3-2 victory at Old Trafford ended a nine-match winless run and lifted the Red Devils to 17th in the 36-team league standings, with six points from their opening four matches.

However, United are only two points above the elimination places at the halfway stage, having suffered consecutive defeats to Atletico Madrid and Como before their recovery against Roma.

With four fixtures remaining, including a daunting encounter with Bayern Munich, the question is how many more points Carrick's men need to secure a place in the knockout rounds.

The results of the previous two Champions League campaigns offer a useful indication, although the eventual qualification threshold will depend on how the other 35 teams perform.

Under the Champions League's expanded format, the top eight teams progress directly to the round of 16, while those finishing between ninth and 24th enter a two-legged knockout phase play-off.

The bottom 12 clubs are eliminated, with no opportunity to drop into the Europa League.

United currently occupy 17th place with six points, having recorded two victories and two defeats. Their goal difference stands at zero, with eight goals scored and eight conceded.

That places them inside the play-off positions for now, but offers little protection against further setbacks.

In the inaugural 36-team league phase in 2024-25, Club Brugge claimed the final play-off position with 11 points, finishing ahead of Dinamo Zagreb on goal difference.

The qualifying threshold was lower last season, when Benfica finished 24th with nine points, narrowly edging out Marseille on the same total.

Meanwhile, 16 points were enough to secure eighth place and direct qualification for the last 16 in both campaigns.

Those figures provide three possible targets for United.

A single additional victory would take Carrick's side to nine points, matching the lowest successful play-off total recorded under the current format.

However, that would not guarantee qualification, particularly given how tightly contested the lower positions are after four rounds.

Five more points would take United to 11, equalling the 2024-25 threshold, while two victories would leave them on 12.

Reaching 12 points would represent a considerably more encouraging position based on recent history, although even that total cannot be regarded as mathematically sufficient this season.

The task becomes substantially harder if United want to avoid the play-offs altogether.

To reach the 16-point benchmark, they would need another 10 points from a possible 12, meaning three victories and a draw, or four consecutive wins.

There is also an important distinction between qualifying for the play-offs and reaching the last 16.

Finishing anywhere from ninth to 24th would keep United in the competition, but they would still need to win a two-legged tie in February to progress.

For Carrick, securing a play-off place is therefore the more realistic immediate objective, with a top-eight finish requiring a near-perfect second half of the league phase.

United's remaining schedule offers opportunities to collect the points they need, although two of their opponents currently sit above them in the table.

Their next European assignment is a trip to Sporting CP on November 25, with the Portuguese side occupying 10th place on nine points.

The Red Devils then welcome RB Leipzig to Old Trafford on December 8, before hosting Bayern Munich on January 20 and concluding the league phase away to Villarreal on January 27.

Leipzig and Villarreal have each collected only three points from their opening four matches, making those encounters particularly important to United's qualification prospects.

Two victories against those opponents would take Carrick's side to 12 points, even if they failed to collect anything from their meetings with Sporting and Bayern.

That would have been enough to reach the play-offs in both previous editions, though United's final position this season would still depend on other results.

The Sporting fixture could also prove significant. A positive result in Lisbon would reduce the pressure on United ahead of their December home match and potentially strengthen their position against a direct rival for the knockout places.

Their January meeting with Bayern presents a different challenge, particularly given the German champions' attacking quality and European experience.

United's situation is also notably less comfortable than that of several other English clubs.

Arsenal have accumulated 10 points, while Aston Villa, Manchester City and Liverpool each have nine, leaving United as the lowest-ranked Premier League representative in the competition.

Elsewhere, Napoli sit 27th with three points, while Atletico Madrid and Roma are also in danger of missing out on the play-offs after collecting four points apiece.

For United, the victory over Roma has provided valuable breathing space, but the margin remains narrow.

Another six points would take them to 12, a total that has historically been sufficient to survive the league phase. Their next two matches, against Sporting and Leipzig, could therefore go a long way towards determining whether the Bayern encounter becomes a battle for qualification or an opportunity to chase a top-eight finish.
